# Manage Your Network with AI Agents

Ella Core ships with an [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io/) that lets AI agents manage your mobile network using natural language. The skill provides the OpenAPI specification so agents can discover and call the REST API on your behalf.

## Prerequisites

Before using the skill, you need:

1. **A running Ella Core instance** with its API accessible (e.g. `http://192.168.1.10:5000`).
1. **A user for your AI agent with an API token**. Create a user for your agent in the UI with a role that matches the permissions you want to grant. Then generate an API token for that user and copy it.

## 1. Install the skill

```
/plugin marketplace add ellanetworks/core
/plugin install ella-core@ellanetworks-core
```

Refresh later with `/plugin marketplace update`.

Works with any Skills-aware tool that auto-discovers `.agents/skills/` (Codex, Cursor, Cline, Goose, Amp, OpenCode, …).

```
npx skills add ellanetworks/core
```

Copy the [`skills/ella-core/`](https://github.com/ellanetworks/core/tree/main/skills/ella-core) folder into the skills directory your AI tool discovers.

## 2. Prompt the agent

Once the skill is active, you can ask things like "Which subscribers used the most data over the last 7 days?". The agent will ask you for the Ella Core URL and an API token. Use the token you generated earlier.

Claude Opus responds to "Which subscribers used the most data over the last 7 days?" using its Ella Core skill.

# Backup and Restore

Ella Core stores all persistent data in an embedded database. You can create backups of this database to protect your data and restore it in case of data loss.

## Backup

1. Open Ella Core in your web browser.
1. Navigate to the **Backup and Restore** tab in the left-hand menu.
1. Click on the **Backup** button.
1. The backup file will be downloaded to your computer. It contains sensitive data, store and transfer it encrypted.

Note

This operation can also be done using the API. Please see the [backup API documentation](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/api/backup/index.md) for more information.

## Restore on same instance

Restoring on the same instance will overwrite all existing data in your Ella Core installation. It is only supported on standalone deployments. For High Availability deployment, see the disaster recovery procedure.

1. Open Ella Core in your web browser.
1. Navigate to the **Backup and Restore** tab in the left-hand menu.
1. Click on the **Upload File** button.
1. Select the backup file you want to restore.

Note

This operation can also be done using the API. Please see the [restore API documentation](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/api/restore/index.md) for more information.

## Offline Restore (Disaster Recovery)

This procedure can be used on new instances.

Paths below assume the default data directory `/var/snap/ella-core/common/data` (the directory holding `db.path`).

1. Stop the daemon on every node in the cluster, or the single standalone node:

   ```
   sudo snap stop ella-core.cored
   ```

1. On the node you seed from the backup, delete the old cluster state:

   ```
   sudo rm -rf /var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db \
               /var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db-wal \
               /var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db-shm \
               /var/snap/ella-core/common/data/raft \
               /var/snap/ella-core/common/data/cluster-tls
   ```

1. Drop the backup archive into the data directory as `restore.bundle`:

   ```
   sudo cp backup.tar.gz /var/snap/ella-core/common/data/restore.bundle
   sudo chmod 600 /var/snap/ella-core/common/data/restore.bundle
   ```

1. Start the daemon on that node:

   ```
   sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored
   ```

1. For a Standalone deployment, stop here.

1. On each remaining node, repeat step 2, then add it via the [join-token flow](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md).

Ella Core includes an embedded BGP speaker that advertises `/32` (IPv4) or `/64` (IPv6) routes for each active subscriber. This guide walks through enabling BGP, adding a peer, and verifying the configuration.

NAT must be disabled

Ella Core does not advertise the IPv4 addresses of subscribers on a data network with NAT, nor the addresses of subscribers on a network instance other than `default`. Disable NAT on the data networks to advertise, in the **Slices** section of each data network's page, before proceeding.

## Enable BGP

1. Open the Ella Core UI and navigate to **Networking > BGP**.
1. Edit the BGP settings:
   - **Local AS**: Your autonomous system number (e.g. `64512`).
   - **Router ID**: A unique IPv4 address identifying this BGP speaker. Leave it empty to use the N6 interface current IPv4 address (e.g. `192.168.5.10`).
   - **Listen Address**: The address and port to listen on (default `:179`). Leave the address empty to accept sessions on every interface, or set one to restrict the speaker to it. Change the port only if you need BGP on a non-standard one. When VRFs are in use, this address also scopes peer connections: set it to an address on a VRF-enslaved interface and both the listener and all peers are bound to that VRF; leave it empty and both follow the N6 interface's VRF.
1. Click **Save**.
1. Toggle **BGP** to **ON**.

## Add a BGP peer

1. In the **Networking > BGP** tab, scroll to the **Peers** section.
1. Click **Create**.
1. Fill in the peer details:
   - **Address**: The IP address of the upstream router (e.g. `192.168.5.1` or `2001:db8::1`).
   - **Remote AS**: The AS number of the peer (e.g. `64513`).
   - **Hold Time**: BGP hold timer in seconds (default `90`). The keepalive interval is derived as hold time / 3 per RFC 4271.
   - **Password** (optional): MD5 authentication password. Must match the peer's configuration.
   - **Description** (optional): A label for the peer.
1. Click **Create**.

## Verify advertised routes

View the advertised subscriber routes in the **Advertised Routes** table. The next-hop is always the N6 interface address.

## Configure the upstream router

Ella Core advertises routes, and can receive them from peers via each peer's import prefixes. You still need to configure the upstream router to:

1. Peer with Ella Core (matching the AS number and address configured above).
1. Accept all routes for subscriber data networks (e.g. `192.168.0.0/24` or `2001:db8::/32`)
1. Accept framed-route prefixes, if any are configured (e.g. `192.168.60.0/24`).

Consult your router's documentation for BGP peering configuration.

Note

All steps in this guide can also be performed via the REST API. See the [BGP API reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/api/networking/#bgp) for details.

# Co-host with Ella IMS and Ella SMSC

This guide runs [Ella IMS](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/) and [Ella SMSC](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/) on the same host as Ella Core. Ella IMS runs in its own network namespace, which Ella Core reaches through an N6 network instance.

## Prerequisites

To follow this guide, you will need:

- A host with Ella Core installed with the snap, as in [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/install/index.md), and an `eth0` interface towards the radio and the internet.
- A free address on the LAN for Ella IMS's UI.

The examples use these values:

| Value                               | Role                                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `eth0`                              | Host interface: N2, N3, N6, and the Ella Core and Ella SMSC UIs |
| `10.3.0.2`                          | Ella Core's Diameter address                                    |
| `10.3.0.7`                          | Ella SMSC's Diameter address                                    |
| `10.6.0.2`                          | Ella Core's address on the `ims` network instance               |
| `10.6.0.5`                          | Ella IMS's SIP and Diameter address                             |
| `192.168.1.50/24`                   | Ella IMS's UI address on the LAN                                |
| `192.168.1.1`                       | LAN gateway                                                     |
| `10.46.0.0/16`                      | IP pool of the `ims` data network                               |
| `001` / `01`                        | Ella Core's MCC and MNC                                         |
| `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org` | Ella Core's Diameter realm                                      |
| `+15550000000`                      | Ella SMSC's service centre address                              |
| `15550000100`                       | Ella IMS's IP-SM-GW number                                      |

## 1. Create the Ella IMS network namespace

Create `/etc/systemd/system/ims-netns.service`:

```
[Unit]
Description=Ella IMS network namespace
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=true

ExecStartPre=-ip netns delete ims
ExecStartPre=-ip link delete diameter0
ExecStart=ip link add diameter0 type dummy
ExecStart=ip addr add 10.3.0.2/32 dev diameter0
ExecStart=ip addr add 10.3.0.7/32 dev diameter0
ExecStart=ip link set diameter0 up
ExecStart=ip netns add ims
ExecStart=ip link add n6-ims type veth peer name ims0
ExecStart=ip link set ims0 netns ims
ExecStart=ip addr add 10.6.0.2/24 dev n6-ims
ExecStart=ip link set n6-ims up
ExecStart=ip link add lan0 link eth0 type macvlan mode bridge
ExecStart=ip link set lan0 netns ims
ExecStart=ip -n ims link set lo up
ExecStart=ip -n ims addr add 10.6.0.5/24 dev ims0
ExecStart=ip -n ims link set ims0 up
ExecStart=ip -n ims addr add 192.168.1.50/24 dev lan0
ExecStart=ip -n ims link set lan0 up
ExecStart=ip -n ims route add default via 192.168.1.1 dev lan0
ExecStart=ip -n ims route add 10.3.0.0/24 via 10.6.0.2 dev ims0
ExecStart=ip -n ims route add 10.46.0.0/16 via 10.6.0.2 dev ims0 mtu lock 1400
ExecStart=ip netns exec ims ethtool -K ims0 tso off gso off tx off
ExecStop=-ip netns delete ims
ExecStop=-ip link delete diameter0

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Enable and start the service:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now ims-netns.service
```

## 2. Configure Ella Core

Edit `/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml`:

```
logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "eth0"
  n3:
    name: "eth0"
  n6:
    name: "eth0"
  network-instances:
    - name: "ims"
      n6:
        name: "n6-ims"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
  diameter:
    address: "10.3.0.2"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
telemetry:
  enabled: false
```

Create `/etc/systemd/system/snap.ella-core.cored.service.d/override.conf`:

```
[Unit]
Requires=ims-netns.service
After=ims-netns.service
```

Restart Ella Core:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo snap restart ella-core.cored
```

## 3. Install Ella IMS in the namespace

Install Ella IMS:

```
sudo snap install ella-ims
sudo snap connect ella-ims:network-control
```

Edit `/var/snap/ella-ims/common/ims.yaml` and set its addresses:

```
api:
  address: 0.0.0.0
  port: 5020
sip:
  addresses: [10.6.0.5]
diameter:
  address: 10.6.0.5
```

Create `/etc/systemd/system/snap.ella-ims.imsd.service.d/override.conf`:

```
[Unit]
Requires=ims-netns.service
After=ims-netns.service

[Service]
NetworkNamespacePath=/var/run/netns/ims
```

Start Ella IMS:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo snap start --enable ella-ims.imsd
```

Ella IMS's UI is at `http://192.168.1.50:5020`.

## 4. Install Ella SMSC

Install Ella SMSC:

```
sudo snap install ella-smsc
```

Edit `/var/snap/ella-smsc/common/smsc.yaml` and set its Diameter address:

```
diameter:
  address: 10.3.0.7
```

Create `/etc/systemd/system/snap.ella-smsc.smscd.service.d/override.conf`:

```
[Unit]
Requires=ims-netns.service
After=ims-netns.service
```

Start Ella SMSC:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo snap start --enable ella-smsc.smscd
```

Ella SMSC's UI is at `http://<eth0 address>:5010`.

## 5. Connect Ella IMS to Ella Core

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **Operator** page:

- Click the edit icon next to **Operator ID (MCC/MNC)**, enter `001` / `01`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Numbering Plan**, enter your country code and prefixes, and click **Update**.

Go to the **Cores** page:

- Under **Peers**, click **Add Peer**, enter `10.3.0.2`, check **HSS** and **PCRF**, and click **Add**.
- Under **HSS**, click the edit icon next to **HSS Realm**, enter `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.
- Under **Voice QoS**, click the edit icon next to **Policy Function**, select **PCRF**, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **PCRF Realm**, enter `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and click **Update**.

## 6. Connect Ella SMSC to Ella Core

In the Ella SMSC UI, go to the **Operator** page:

- Click the edit icon next to **Operator ID (MCC/MNC)**, enter `001` / `01`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Service Centre Address**, enter `+15550000000`, and click **Update**.
- Click the edit icon next to **Numbering**, enter your country code and prefixes, and click **Update**.

Go to the **Diameter** page and note the **Host**, e.g. `smsc.node.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`.

In the Ella Core UI, go to **Integrations › SMS**. Click the edit icon next to **Serving Node Number**, enter Ella Core's E.164 number for SMS, e.g. `+15550001111`, and click **Update**. Then click **Add SMSC** and enter:

- **Name**: `smsc`
- **Service Centre Addresses**: `+15550000000`
- **Address**: `10.3.0.7`
- **Origin-Host**: Ella SMSC's **Host**.

Click **Add**.

## 7. Enable SMS over IP

In the Ella IMS UI, go to the **Cores** page:

- Under **SMS over IP**, click the edit icon next to **IP-SM-GW Number**, enter `15550000100`, and click **Update**. Note the **IP-SM-GW Name**.
- Under **Peers**, click **Add Peer**, and enter:
  - **Address**: `10.3.0.7`
  - **Roles**: **SGd** only
  - **Service Centres**: `15550000000`
  - **Transport**: **SCTP**
  - **Host**: Ella SMSC's **Host**.
- Click **Add**.
- Click the edit icon of the `10.3.0.2` peer, check **Sh**, **S6c** and **SGd**, and click **Update**.

In the Ella Core UI, go to **Integrations › IMS**:

- Click **Add Application Server**, enter `ip-sm-gw` as the **Name** and Ella IMS's **IP-SM-GW Name** as the **Server Name**, and click **Add**.
- Click **Add Service Profile**, enter `sms-over-ip` as the **Name**. Under **Add from preset**, select the **SMS over IP** preset and the `ip-sm-gw` **Application Server**, click **Add Criteria**, and click **Add**.

## 8. Route the `ims` data network to Ella IMS

In the Ella Core UI:

1. Go to **Networking > Data Networks**, click **Create**, enter `ims` as the **Name** and `10.46.0.0/16` as the **IPv4 Pool**, turn on **IMS (voice and mission critical services)**, and click **Create**.
1. Open the `ims` data network. In **Slices**, select the slice of your subscribers and click **Serve on slice**, then set its **Network instance** to `ims`.
1. Go to **Integrations › IMS**, click the edit icon next to **P-CSCF Addresses**, enter `10.6.0.5`, and click **Update**.

## 9. Set up the subscribers

In the Ella Core UI, for each profile whose subscribers make calls and send SMS:

- Go to the **Profiles** page and open the profile.
- Click **Add Policy**, enter a **Name**, set the **Data Network** to `ims`, and click **Create**.
- Click the edit icon next to **IMS Service Profiles**, set **MMTel (voice, SMS)** to `sms-over-ip`, and click **Save**.

For each subscriber, go to the **Subscribers** page, open the subscriber, click the edit icon next to **MSISDN**, enter its E.164 number, e.g. `+15551230001`, and click **Update**.

On each SIM card, set the SMSC number to `+15550000000`. On each phone, turn on VoLTE (4G) or VoNR (5G).

## 10. Verify

- In the Ella Core UI, go to **Networking > Interfaces**: the **N6 (External) · ims** card shows `n6-ims`, used by `ims`.
- In the Ella IMS UI, go to **Cores**: under **Peers**, `10.3.0.2` and `10.3.0.7` show **open**.
- In the Ella SMSC UI, go to **Diameter**: under **Connected Peers**, Ella Core and Ella IMS show **open**.
- In the Ella Core UI, go to **Subscribers** and open a subscriber with an MSISDN: **Voice** shows **Registered**.
- Call a phone from another. The call connects with audio in both directions.
- Send an SMS between two phones. In the Ella SMSC UI, on the **Messages** page, it shows **delivered**.

# Co-host with OCUDU

Ella Core can be hosted with radio software like [OCUDU](https://ocudu.org/) (previously known as srsRAN) to operate an all-in-one private mobile network. This guide provides step-by-step instructions to deploy Ella Core alongside OCUDU using a Linux network namespace.

Co-host Ella Core with OCUDU

Note

The same instructions can be used to co-host Ella Core with [srsRAN 4G](https://www.srsran.com/4g).

## Pre-requisites

To follow this guide, you will need:

- Ubuntu Server 26.04
- A host with a wired network interface
- A USB, UHD-compatible SDR

The instructions below were written for a Raspberry Pi 5 running Ubuntu 26.04 and the Ettus Research B205-mini SDR. Please adapt the interface names and SDR configuration as needed for your setup.

Tip

OCUDU requires some performance tuning for stable operation, especially on resource-constrained hosts like a Raspberry Pi. We recommend the following optimizations for OCUDU performance:

- Use Ubuntu Real-Time (following [documentation](https://ubuntu.com/real-time/docs/how-to/enable-real-time-ubuntu/))
- Use a high real-time scheduling priority (with [chrt](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/chrt.1.html))

## 1. Install Ella Core and OCUDU

Install Ella Core using the [How-to Install guide](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/install/index.md) and install OCUDU using the snap:

```
sudo snap install ocudu
sudo snap connect ocudu:kernel-module-observe
sudo snap connect ocudu:process-control
sudo snap connect ocudu:network-control
sudo snap connect ocudu:system-observe
sudo snap connect ocudu:raw-usb
```

## 2. Create a network namespace for N3

Create a linux network namespace `n3ns` for the N3 interface between OCUDU and Ella Core.

Install the OCUDU performance script:

```
sudo curl -o /usr/local/bin/ocudu_performance https://gitlab.com/ocudu/ocudu/-/raw/dev/scripts/ocudu_performance
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/ocudu_performance
```

Create `/etc/systemd/system/n3ns.service`:

```
[Unit]
Description=N3 Network Setup
Wants=network-online.target
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=true

ExecStartPre=-ip netns delete n3ns
ExecStart=ip netns add n3ns
ExecStart=ip link add n3-upf-veth type veth peer name n3-ran-veth
ExecStart=ip link set n3-ran-veth netns n3ns
ExecStart=ip addr add 10.202.0.3/24 dev n3-upf-veth
ExecStart=ip -n n3ns addr add 10.202.0.5/24 dev n3-ran-veth
ExecStart=ip -n n3ns link set lo up
ExecStart=ip -n n3ns link set dev n3-ran-veth up
ExecStart=ip link set dev n3-upf-veth up
ExecStart=ip netns exec n3ns ethtool -K n3-ran-veth tso off gso off
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/ocudu_performance -y
ExecStop=-ip netns delete n3ns

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

Enable and start the service:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now n3ns.service
```

Make sure `eth0` is not optional in `/etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml`:

```
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    eth0:
      dhcp4: true
      optional: false
```

Apply the Netplan configuration:

```
sudo netplan apply
```

## 3. Configure Ella Core

Configure Ella Core's N3 and N3 interfaces to use the `n3ns` namespace and set N6 to the physical interface `eth0`:

```
logging:
  system:
    level: "debug"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "n3-upf-veth"
    ngap-port: 38412
  n3:
    name: "n3-upf-veth"
  n6:
    name: "eth0"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
telemetry:
  enabled: false
```

Note

We use `tcx` mode here because the Raspberry Pi 5 does not support native XDP. Use `xdp-native` if you can and follow the [Use native XDP with veth interfaces](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/native_xdp_veth/index.md) guide to attach an XDP program to the peer veth.

Create the override file `/etc/systemd/system/snap.ella-core.cored.service.d/override.conf`:

```
[Unit]
Requires=n3ns.service
Wants=network-online.target
After=n3ns.service network-online.target
```

Reload systemd and start Ella Core:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored
```

## 4. Configure OCUDU

Configure OCUDU's CU to use the `n3ns` namespace:

```
cu_cp:
  amf:
    addr: 10.202.0.3
    port: 38412
    bind_addr: 10.202.0.5
    supported_tracking_areas:
      - tac: 1
        plmn_list:
          - plmn: "99901"
            tai_slice_support_list:
              - sst: 1
  inactivity_timer: 300
  security:
    nea_pref_list: nea2,nea1
    nia_pref_list: nia2,nia1
cu_up:
  ngu:
    socket:
      - bind_addr: 10.202.0.5
ru_sdr:
  device_driver: uhd
  device_args: type=b200
  clock: internal
  srate: 23.04
  tx_gain: 80
  rx_gain: 40

cell_cfg:
  dl_arfcn: 665000
  band: 77
  channel_bandwidth_MHz: 20
  common_scs: 30
  plmn: "99901"
  tac: 1
  pdcch:
    dedicated:
      ss2_type: common
      dci_format_0_1_and_1_1: false
  prach:
    prach_config_index: 160
  pdsch:
    mcs_table: qam64
  pusch:
    mcs_table: qam64

log:
  filename: stdout
  all_level: warning

pcap:
  mac_enable: disable
  ngap_enable: disable
```

Save this configuration to `/var/snap/ocudu/common/gnb.yml`.

Override the ocudu `gnb` service by writing `/etc/systemd/system/snap.ocudu.gnb.service.d/override.conf`:

```
[Service]
NetworkNamespacePath=/var/run/netns/n3ns
```

Enable and start OCUDU:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo snap start --enable ocudu.gnb
```

You should see the LEDs light up on your USRP, and see the radio appear in Ella Core's UI.

You can validate OCUDU is running properly by looking at the logs:

```
sudo snap logs ocudu -n 1000 -f
```

# Configure Roaming

This page has two guides: 5G roaming and 4G roaming. Each adds a roaming partner, so the partner's subscribers can attach to Ella Core. To learn how roaming works, see [Roaming](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/roaming/index.md).

## 5G roaming

### Prerequisites

- **Data networks and slices**: a data network named after each DNN that the partner's subscribers use, e.g. `internet` (names match regardless of letter case), and slices with the S-NSSAI values of their subscriptions, each serving these data networks.
- **Partner subscriptions**: the partner allows local breakout for these data networks in its subscriptions.

### 1. Enable the N32 interface

On each node, set `interfaces.n32` in the [configuration file](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/config_file/index.md) to the interface that reaches the partner's SEPP:

```
interfaces:
  n32:
    address: "192.0.2.11"
    port: 443
```

Restart Ella Core.

### 2. Exchange information with the partner

On each node, go to **Integrations › Roaming**. Under **This Core**, note the SEPP FQDN from the **Certificate** row, and the **N32 Address**.

Give the partner:

| Item                                                        | Example                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Your PLMN ID                                                | `001/01`                                                    |
| Each node's SEPP FQDN and N32 address                       | `sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, `192.0.2.11:443` |
| The trust anchors, downloaded from the **Trust anchor** row | `sepp-ca.pem`                                               |

Get from the partner:

| Item                                     | Example                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Its PLMN IDs                             | `999/70`                                              |
| Its SEPP FQDN                            | `sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org`             |
| Its N32-c URI                            | `https://sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org:443` |
| Its trust anchor                         | `partner-ca.pem`                                      |
| The NRF API root of each of its PLMN IDs | `https://nrf.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org`       |

Configure DNS so that Ella Core resolves the partner's SEPP FQDN, and the partner resolves each node's SEPP FQDN.

### 3. Create a profile for roamers

Go to the **Profiles** page and create a profile named `roamers`, with **5G** access.

Add a policy on each data network that roamers may use, e.g. `internet`.

### 4. Add the partner

In **Integrations › Roaming**, open **Partners** and click **Add Partner**:

- **Name**: e.g. `Partner Telecom`.
- **MCC** and **MNC**: the partner's PLMN ID, e.g. `999` and `70`. Click **Add PLMN** for each other PLMN ID of the partner.
- **Profile**: `roamers`.
- **5G Roaming**: turn on, and enter the partner's **SEPP FQDN**, **N32-c URI**, **Trust Anchor**, and the **NRF API Root** of each PLMN ID.

Click **Create**.

### 5. Verify

On each node, in **Integrations › Roaming**, the partner shows **Established** in the **N32 Status** column of **Partners**.

Register a 5G UE with a SIM of the partner's network, with data roaming on. Open the **Roamers** tab of the **Subscribers** page of the node that serves it: the roamer appears, with its roaming partner.

## 4G roaming

### Prerequisites

- **Data networks**: a data network named after each APN that the partner's subscribers use, e.g. `internet` (names match regardless of letter case), served on a slice.
- **Partner subscriptions**: the partner allows local breakout for these APNs in its subscriptions.

### 1. Exchange information with the partner

Give the partner:

| Item                                                                         | Example                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Your PLMN ID                                                                 | `001/01`                                                 |
| The **Diameter Realm**, from **Integrations › Roaming**, under **This Core** | `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`                      |
| Each node's **Origin-Host**, from the same place                             | `mmec01.mmegi0001.mme.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org` |
| Each node's Diameter address and port (`interfaces.diameter`)                | `192.0.2.11`, `3868`                                     |

Get from the partner:

| Item                                                        | Example                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| Its PLMN IDs                                                | `999/70`               |
| The address and SCTP port of its HSS or Diameter Edge Agent | `198.51.100.5`, `3868` |

### 2. Create a profile for roamers

Go to the **Profiles** page and create a profile named `roamers`, with **4G** access.

Add a policy on each data network that roamers may use, e.g. `internet`.

### 3. Add the Diameter peer

In **Integrations › Roaming**, open **Diameter Peers** and click **Add Diameter Peer**:

- **Address**: the partner's HSS or Diameter Edge Agent, e.g. `198.51.100.5`.
- **Port**: e.g. `3868`.

Click **Create**.

### 4. Add the partner

Open **Partners** and click **Add Partner**:

- **Name**: e.g. `Partner Telecom`.
- **MCC** and **MNC**: the partner's PLMN ID, e.g. `999` and `70`. Click **Add PLMN** for each other PLMN ID of the partner.
- **Profile**: `roamers`.
- **4G Roaming**: turn on, and select the Diameter peer from step 3.

Click **Create**.

### 5. Verify

On each node, in **Integrations › Roaming**, the partner's Diameter peer shows **Connected** under **Diameter Peers**.

Attach a 4G UE with a SIM of the partner's network, with data roaming on. Open the **Roamers** tab of the **Subscribers** page of the node that serves it: the roamer appears, with its roaming partner.

Note

All steps in this guide can also be performed via the REST API. See the [Integrations API reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/api/integrations/#list-roaming-partners) for details.

# Deploy a High Availability Cluster

Ella Core can be deployed as a high-availability cluster to provide redundancy and failover capabilities. See [High Availability](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/high_availability/index.md) for more information.

## Prerequisites

- Three hosts meeting the standard [system requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/system_reqs/index.md).
- Ella Core installed on each host via the [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/install/index.md) guide with `cluster.bind-address` set in the configuration file.

## 1. Start node 1

Start node 1, open a browser at the API address and initialize it normally.

## 2. Create a join token for node 2

Still in node 1, open the **Cluster** page and click **Add Node**, click **Mint Token**, then copy the token.

## 3. Start node 2

Start node 2, open a browser at the API address and click **Join an existing cluster instead**. Paste the token, enter node 1's cluster address, and click **Join**.

## 4. Add node 3

Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node 3.

## 5. Verify

On the **Cluster** page, all three nodes appear as **Healthy**.

# Deploy in the Cloud

Run Ella Core in the cloud while your radios stay on site. Deploy a three-node cluster across three zones and connect a radio to it over IPsec.

Note

This guide uses cloud instances. Ella Core can also run on managed Kubernetes, such as GKE or EKS.

Ella Core running in Google Cloud

Ella Core running in AWS

Ella Core running in Azure

## Prerequisites

- A radio that supports IPsec and several MME or AMF addresses. Without IPsec on the radio, use an IPsec router at the site.

- A Google Cloud project and the `gcloud` CLI.

The examples use `203.0.113.10` for the site's public address, `192.168.1.50` for the radio, and `10.128.0.0/20` for the `default` subnet in `us-central1`.

- An AWS account and the `aws` CLI.

The examples use `203.0.113.10` for the site's public address, `192.168.1.50` for the radio, and the default VPC (`172.31.0.0/16`) in `us-east-1`.

- An Azure subscription and the `az` CLI, with the `bastion` and `ssh` extensions.
- An SSH key at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.

The examples use `203.0.113.10` for the site's public address, `192.168.1.50` for the radio, and `10.10.0.0/16` for the virtual network in `eastus`.

## 1. Prepare the project

Set the project and region:

```
gcloud config set project <project>
R="--region us-central1"
```

Allow the radio to reach Ella Core:

```
gcloud compute firewall-rules create ella-core-allow-radio --network default \
  --allow sctp:36412,sctp:38412,udp:2152,icmp \
  --source-ranges 192.168.1.50/32 --target-tags ella-core
```

Allow the nodes to reach each other:

```
gcloud compute firewall-rules create ella-core-allow-cluster --network default \
  --allow tcp:7000 --source-tags ella-core --target-tags ella-core
```

Allow Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) to reach SSH and the UI:

```
gcloud compute firewall-rules create ella-core-allow-iap --network default \
  --allow tcp:22,tcp:5002 --source-ranges 35.235.240.0/20 --target-tags ella-core
```

Give the instances internet access:

```
gcloud compute routers create ella-nat-router --network default $R
gcloud compute routers nats create ella-nat --router ella-nat-router $R \
  --auto-allocate-nat-external-ips --nat-all-subnet-ip-ranges
```

Set the region and find the default VPC:

```
export AWS_REGION=us-east-1
VPC=$(aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=isDefault,Values=true --query 'Vpcs[0].VpcId' --output text)
```

Allow the radio to reach Ella Core, and the nodes to reach each other:

```
SG=$(aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name ella-core --description "Ella Core" --vpc-id $VPC --query GroupId --output text)
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $SG --ip-permissions \
  'IpProtocol=132,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=192.168.1.50/32}]' \
  'IpProtocol=udp,FromPort=2152,ToPort=2152,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=192.168.1.50/32}]' \
  'IpProtocol=icmp,FromPort=-1,ToPort=-1,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=192.168.1.50/32}]' \
  "IpProtocol=tcp,FromPort=7000,ToPort=7000,UserIdGroupPairs=[{GroupId=$SG}]"
```

Allow Session Manager to reach the instances:

```
aws iam create-role --role-name ella-core-ssm --assume-role-policy-document \
  '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"Service":"ec2.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}'
aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name ella-core-ssm --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore
aws iam create-instance-profile --instance-profile-name ella-core-ssm
aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name ella-core-ssm --role-name ella-core-ssm
```

Create the resource group:

```
az group create -n ella-core -l eastus
G="-g ella-core"
```

Create the virtual network, with subnets for the instances, the VPN gateway and Bastion:

```
az network vnet create $G -n ella-vnet --address-prefixes 10.10.0.0/16 --subnet-name ella --subnet-prefixes 10.10.1.0/24
az network vnet subnet create $G --vnet-name ella-vnet -n GatewaySubnet --address-prefixes 10.10.255.0/27
az network vnet subnet create $G --vnet-name ella-vnet -n AzureBastionSubnet --address-prefixes 10.10.254.0/26
```

Give the instances internet access:

```
az network public-ip create $G -n ella-nat-ip --sku StandardV2 --allocation-method Static
az network nat gateway create $G -n ella-nat --sku StandardV2 --public-ip-addresses ella-nat-ip
az network vnet subnet update $G --vnet-name ella-vnet -n ella --nat-gateway ella-nat
```

Create a Bastion host to reach SSH and the UI:

```
az network public-ip create $G -n ella-bastion-ip --sku Standard
az network bastion create $G -n ella-bastion --vnet-name ella-vnet --public-ip-address ella-bastion-ip \
  --sku Standard --enable-tunneling
```

## 2. Create the VPN gateway

Create a Classic VPN gateway:

```
gcloud compute addresses create radio-vpn-ip $R
GW=$(gcloud compute addresses describe radio-vpn-ip $R --format='value(address)')
echo $GW
gcloud compute target-vpn-gateways create radio-vpn --network default $R
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create radio-vpn-esp $R --address $GW --target-vpn-gateway radio-vpn --ip-protocol ESP
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create radio-vpn-udp500 $R --address $GW --target-vpn-gateway radio-vpn --ip-protocol UDP --ports 500
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create radio-vpn-udp4500 $R --address $GW --target-vpn-gateway radio-vpn --ip-protocol UDP --ports 4500
```

Create a pre-shared key, the tunnel, and a route to the radio:

```
head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=' | head -c 32 > radio-vpn.psk
gcloud compute vpn-tunnels create radio-tunnel $R --target-vpn-gateway radio-vpn \
  --peer-address 203.0.113.10 --ike-version 2 --shared-secret "$(cat radio-vpn.psk)" \
  --local-traffic-selector 10.128.0.0/20 --remote-traffic-selector 192.168.1.50/32
gcloud compute routes create radio-route --network default --destination-range 192.168.1.50/32 \
  --next-hop-vpn-tunnel radio-tunnel --next-hop-vpn-tunnel-region us-central1
```

Create a virtual private gateway and attach it to the VPC:

```
VGW=$(aws ec2 create-vpn-gateway --type ipsec.1 --query VpnGateway.VpnGatewayId --output text)
aws ec2 attach-vpn-gateway --vpn-gateway-id $VGW --vpc-id $VPC
until [ "$(aws ec2 describe-vpn-gateways --vpn-gateway-ids $VGW --query 'VpnGateways[0].VpcAttachments[0].State' --output text)" = attached ]; do sleep 5; done
RT=$(aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC Name=association.main,Values=true --query 'RouteTables[0].RouteTableId' --output text)
aws ec2 enable-vgw-route-propagation --route-table-id $RT --gateway-id $VGW
```

Create a customer gateway for the site, a pre-shared key, the VPN connection, and a route to the radio:

```
CGW=$(aws ec2 create-customer-gateway --type ipsec.1 --ip-address 203.0.113.10 --bgp-asn 65000 --query CustomerGateway.CustomerGatewayId --output text)
head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=' | head -c 31 | sed 's/^/k/' > radio-vpn.psk
T='{"IKEVersions":[{"Value":"ikev2"}],"PreSharedKey":"'$(cat radio-vpn.psk)'","Phase1EncryptionAlgorithms":[{"Value":"AES256"}],"Phase2EncryptionAlgorithms":[{"Value":"AES256"}],"Phase1IntegrityAlgorithms":[{"Value":"SHA2-256"}],"Phase2IntegrityAlgorithms":[{"Value":"SHA2-256"}],"Phase1DHGroupNumbers":[{"Value":14}],"Phase2DHGroupNumbers":[{"Value":14}]}'
VPN=$(aws ec2 create-vpn-connection --type ipsec.1 --customer-gateway-id $CGW --vpn-gateway-id $VGW \
  --options '{"StaticRoutesOnly":true,"LocalIpv4NetworkCidr":"192.168.1.50/32","RemoteIpv4NetworkCidr":"172.31.0.0/16","TunnelOptions":['"$T,$T"']}' \
  --query VpnConnection.VpnConnectionId --output text)
aws ec2 create-vpn-connection-route --vpn-connection-id $VPN --destination-cidr-block 192.168.1.50/32
GW=$(aws ec2 describe-vpn-connections --vpn-connection-ids $VPN --query 'VpnConnections[0].VgwTelemetry[0].OutsideIpAddress' --output text)
echo $GW
```

Create the VPN gateway. This can take 45 minutes:

```
az network public-ip create $G -n radio-vpn-ip --sku Standard --zone 1 2 3
az network vnet-gateway create $G -n radio-vpn --vnet ella-vnet --public-ip-addresses radio-vpn-ip \
  --gateway-type Vpn --vpn-type RouteBased --sku VpnGw1AZ
GW=$(az network public-ip show $G -n radio-vpn-ip --query ipAddress -o tsv)
echo $GW
```

Create a local network gateway for the site, a pre-shared key, and the connection:

```
az network local-gateway create $G -n radio-site --gateway-ip-address 203.0.113.10 --local-address-prefixes 192.168.1.50/32
head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -d '/+=' | head -c 32 > radio-vpn.psk
az network vpn-connection create $G -n radio-tunnel --vnet-gateway1 radio-vpn --local-gateway2 radio-site \
  --shared-key "$(cat radio-vpn.psk)"
az network vpn-connection ipsec-policy add $G --connection-name radio-tunnel \
  --ike-encryption AES256 --ike-integrity SHA256 --dh-group DHGroup14 \
  --ipsec-encryption AES256 --ipsec-integrity SHA256 --pfs-group PFS2048 \
  --sa-lifetime 27000 --sa-max-size 102400000
```

## 3. Create the instances

Create one instance per zone, at `10.128.0.10`, `10.128.0.11` and `10.128.0.12`:

```
i=10
for z in a b c; do
  gcloud compute instances create ella-core-$z --zone us-central1-$z \
    --machine-type e2-standard-2 --subnet default --private-network-ip 10.128.0.$i \
    --no-address --tags ella-core \
    --image-family ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64 --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 20GB
  i=$((i+1))
done
```

Create one instance per availability zone, at the tenth address of the zone's default subnet:

```
AMI=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/canonical/ubuntu/server/24.04/stable/current/amd64/hvm/ebs-gp3/ami-id --query Parameter.Value --output text)
for z in a b c; do
  read SUBNET CIDR <<< "$(aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=$VPC Name=availability-zone,Values=us-east-1$z Name=default-for-az,Values=true --query 'Subnets[0].[SubnetId,CidrBlock]' --output text)"
  ip=${CIDR%.*}.10
  ID=$(aws ec2 run-instances --image-id $AMI --instance-type t3.medium --subnet-id $SUBNET --private-ip-address $ip \
    --security-group-ids $SG --iam-instance-profile Name=ella-core-ssm \
    --block-device-mappings 'DeviceName=/dev/sda1,Ebs={VolumeSize=20,VolumeType=gp3}' \
    --tag-specifications "ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=ella-core-$z}]" \
    --query 'Instances[0].InstanceId' --output text)
  echo "ella-core-$z $ID $ip ${CIDR%.*}.1"
done
```

The output lists each instance's name, ID, address and gateway, e.g.:

```
ella-core-a i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60001 172.31.0.10 172.31.0.1
ella-core-b i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60002 172.31.80.10 172.31.80.1
ella-core-c i-0a1b2c3d4e5f60003 172.31.16.10 172.31.16.1
```

The following steps use these example values.

Create one instance per zone, at `10.10.1.10`, `10.10.1.11` and `10.10.1.12`:

```
i=10
for z in 1 2 3; do
  az vm create $G -n ella-core-$z --zone $z --size Standard_D2as_v7 \
    --image Canonical:ubuntu-24_04-lts:server:latest --vnet-name ella-vnet --subnet ella \
    --private-ip-address 10.10.1.$i --public-ip-address "" --nsg "" \
    --admin-username azureuser --ssh-key-values ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
  i=$((i+1))
done
```

## 4. Install Ella Core

On each instance:

```
gcloud compute ssh ella-core-<z> --zone us-central1-<z> --tunnel-through-iap
```

Limit the size of packets sent to the radio, so they fit in the VPN tunnel:

```
sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens4:
      routes:
        - to: 192.168.1.50/32
          via: 10.128.0.1
          mtu: 1300
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml
sudo netplan apply
```

Install Ella Core:

```
sudo snap install ella-core
```

Replace `/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml` with the following, setting `bind-address` to the instance's address:

```
logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "ens4"
  n3:
    name: "ens4"
  n6:
    name: "ens4"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
cluster:
  bind-address: "10.128.0.10:7000"
```

Start Ella Core:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored
```

On each instance:

```
aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id>
```

Limit the size of packets sent to the radio, so they fit in the VPN tunnel. Set `via` to the instance's gateway from step 3, e.g. `172.31.0.1`:

```
sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens5:
      routes:
        - to: 192.168.1.50/32
          via: 172.31.0.1
          mtu: 1300
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml
sudo netplan apply
```

Install Ella Core:

```
sudo snap install ella-core
```

Replace `/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml` with the following, setting `bind-address` to the instance's address from step 3:

```
logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "ens5"
  n3:
    name: "ens5"
  n6:
    name: "ens5"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
cluster:
  bind-address: "172.31.0.10:7000"
```

Start Ella Core:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored
```

On each instance:

```
az network bastion ssh $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-<z> --query id -o tsv) \
  --auth-type ssh-key --username azureuser --ssh-key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```

Limit the size of packets sent to the radio, so they fit in the VPN tunnel:

```
sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    eth0:
      routes:
        - to: 192.168.1.50/32
          via: 10.10.1.1
          mtu: 1300
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-ella.yaml
sudo netplan apply
```

Install Ella Core:

```
sudo snap install ella-core
```

Replace `/var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml` with the following, setting `bind-address` to the instance's address:

```
logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    name: "eth0"
  n3:
    name: "eth0"
  n6:
    name: "eth0"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "tcx"
cluster:
  bind-address: "10.10.1.10:7000"
```

Start Ella Core:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored
```

## 5. Form the cluster

Open each node's UI through IAP, each in its own terminal:

```
gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel ella-core-a 5002 --local-host-port=localhost:5002 --zone us-central1-a
gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel ella-core-b 5002 --local-host-port=localhost:5003 --zone us-central1-b
gcloud compute start-iap-tunnel ella-core-c 5002 --local-host-port=localhost:5004 --zone us-central1-c
```

1. Open `https://localhost:5002` and initialize node a.
1. Open **Cluster**, click **Add Node**, click **Mint Token**, and copy the token.
1. Open `https://localhost:5003`, click **Join an existing cluster instead**, paste the token, enter `10.128.0.10:7000`, and click **Join**.
1. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node c, at `https://localhost:5004`.

Open each node's UI through Session Manager, each in its own terminal:

```
aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id-a> --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSession --parameters portNumber=5002,localPortNumber=5002
aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id-b> --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSession --parameters portNumber=5002,localPortNumber=5003
aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id-c> --document-name AWS-StartPortForwardingSession --parameters portNumber=5002,localPortNumber=5004
```

1. Open `https://localhost:5002` and initialize node a.
1. Open **Cluster**, click **Add Node**, click **Mint Token**, and copy the token.
1. Open `https://localhost:5003`, click **Join an existing cluster instead**, paste the token, enter node a's address from step 3 with port `7000`, e.g. `172.31.0.10:7000`, and click **Join**.
1. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node c, at `https://localhost:5004`.

Open each node's UI through Bastion, each in its own terminal:

```
az network bastion tunnel $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-1 --query id -o tsv) --resource-port 5002 --port 5002
az network bastion tunnel $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-2 --query id -o tsv) --resource-port 5002 --port 5003
az network bastion tunnel $G -n ella-bastion --target-resource-id $(az vm show $G -n ella-core-3 --query id -o tsv) --resource-port 5002 --port 5004
```

1. Open `https://localhost:5002` and initialize node 1.
1. Open **Cluster**, click **Add Node**, click **Mint Token**, and copy the token.
1. Open `https://localhost:5003`, click **Join an existing cluster instead**, paste the token, enter `10.10.1.10:7000`, and click **Join**.
1. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for node 3, at `https://localhost:5004`.

On the **Cluster** page, the three nodes appear as **Healthy**.

## 6. Configure the network

In the UI:

1. In **Operator**, set the MCC, MNC and TAC to match the radio and SIM cards.
1. In **Data Networks**, open `internet` and set its MTU to `1300`.
1. In **Subscribers**, add each SIM card.

## 7. Connect the radio

Give the radio a static address on the site network, e.g. `192.168.1.50/24` with gateway `192.168.1.1`.

Configure an IPsec tunnel on the radio:

| Setting           | Value                                          |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Peer              | The VPN gateway address (`$GW`)                |
| IKE version       | IKEv2                                          |
| Authentication    | The pre-shared key in `radio-vpn.psk`          |
| Local ID          | The site's public address, e.g. `203.0.113.10` |
| Remote ID         | The VPN gateway address                        |
| Local subnet      | `192.168.1.50/32`                              |
| Remote subnet     | `10.128.0.0/20`                                |
| IKE and ESP       | AES-256, SHA-256, DH group 14 (MODP 2048)      |
| IKE lifetime      | 10 h or less                                   |
| IPsec SA lifetime | 3 h or less                                    |

Set the radio's MME (4G) or AMF (5G) addresses to `10.128.0.10`, `10.128.0.11` and `10.128.0.12`, then restart the radio.

| Setting           | Value                                          |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Peer              | The tunnel's outside address (`$GW`)           |
| IKE version       | IKEv2                                          |
| Authentication    | The pre-shared key in `radio-vpn.psk`          |
| Local ID          | The site's public address, e.g. `203.0.113.10` |
| Remote ID         | The tunnel's outside address                   |
| Local subnet      | `192.168.1.50/32`                              |
| Remote subnet     | `172.31.0.0/16`                                |
| IKE and ESP       | AES-256, SHA-256, DH group 14 (MODP 2048)      |
| IKE lifetime      | 8 h or less                                    |
| IPsec SA lifetime | 1 h or less                                    |

Set the radio's MME (4G) or AMF (5G) addresses to the three instance addresses from step 3, e.g. `172.31.0.10`, `172.31.80.10` and `172.31.16.10`.

| Setting           | Value                                          |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Peer              | The VPN gateway address (`$GW`)                |
| IKE version       | IKEv2                                          |
| Authentication    | The pre-shared key in `radio-vpn.psk`          |
| Local ID          | The site's public address, e.g. `203.0.113.10` |
| Remote ID         | The VPN gateway address                        |
| Local subnet      | `192.168.1.50/32`                              |
| Remote subnet     | `10.10.0.0/16`                                 |
| IKE and ESP       | AES-256, SHA-256, DH group 14 (MODP 2048)      |
| IKE lifetime      | 8 h or less                                    |
| IPsec SA lifetime | 7.5 h or less                                  |

Set the radio's MME (4G) or AMF (5G) addresses to `10.10.1.10`, `10.10.1.11` and `10.10.1.12`, then restart the radio.

## 8. Verify

Check that the tunnel is up:

```
gcloud compute vpn-tunnels describe radio-tunnel $R --format='value(status)'
```

The output is `ESTABLISHED`.

```
aws ec2 describe-vpn-connections --vpn-connection-ids $VPN --query 'VpnConnections[0].VgwTelemetry[0].Status' --output text
```

The output is `UP`.

```
az network vpn-connection show $G -n radio-tunnel --query connectionStatus -o tsv
```

The output is `Connected`.

The radio appears on the **Radios** page, and attached phones appear as **Registered** on the **Subscribers** page.

# Enable MCPTT

This guide shows how to serve Mission Critical Push To Talk (MCPTT) to subscribers over 4G and 5G, with an external IMS and an MCPTT server. To learn how Ella Core works with the IMS, see [IMS Integration](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/ims_integration/index.md).

## Prerequisites

- **IMS**: an IMS integrated with Ella Core, as in [Integrate with an IMS](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/integrate_with_ims/index.md). Its P-CSCF must send the MCPTT ICSI, `urn:urn-7:3gpp-service.ims.icsi.mcptt`, in the AF-Application-Identifier of MCPTT calls.
- **MCPTT server**: [Ella IMS](https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims), set up as in [Enable Push-to-Talk](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/enable_push_to_talk/), or a 3GPP MCPTT server that the IMS reaches and trusts.
- **MCPTT clients**: configured with the MC data network (`mcx` below) as their MC services APN or DNN.
- **Radios**: support for QCI/5QI 69 and 65.
- **SIMs**: with an ISIM you can program.
- **Phones**: an IMS client that registers with a `reg-id`.

## 1. Create the MC data network

In the Ella Core UI, go to the **Networking** page and open the **Data Networks** tab.

Click **Create**, enter `mcx` as the **Name**, set an IP pool, turn on **IMS (voice and mission critical services)**, and click **Create**.

Open the `mcx` data network, and in **Slices**, select the slice of your MCPTT users and click **Serve on slice**.

## 2. Create the MC profile

Go to the **Profiles** page and click **Create**. Enter a **Name**, e.g. `mcptt`, and click **Create**.

Click on the new profile, click **Add Policy**, and set:

- **Data Network**: `mcx`.
- **5QI / QCI**: `69 — Mission critical signalling`.
- **Allocation and Retention Priority (ARP)**: a level between 1 and 8, e.g. `3`.
- **Pre-emption capability**: `May pre-empt`.
- **Pre-emption vulnerability**: `Not pre-emptable`.

Click **Create**.

Also add the policies the MCPTT users have on their current profile, e.g. on `internet` and `ims`.

## 3. Add the MCPTT application server

Go to **Integrations › IMS**. Under **Application Servers**, click **Add Application Server**, click **Fill for Ella IMS MCPTT**, and click **Add**.

With another MCPTT server, enter `mcptt` as the **Name**, its SIP URI as the **Server Name**, and an **Identity** matching its identities, e.g. `sip:!.*!@mcptt.example.org`.

## 4. Create the MCPTT service profile

In **Integrations › IMS**, under **Service Profiles**, click **Add Service Profile**. Enter `mcptt` as the **Name**. Under **Add from preset**, select the `MCPTT` **Preset** and the `mcptt` **Application Server**, and click **Add Criteria**. Click **Add**.

## 5. Give the MC profile the MCPTT service profile

Go to the **Profiles** page and click on the MC profile. Click the edit icon next to **IMS Service Profiles**, select `mcptt` for **MCPTT** and, for **MMTel (voice, SMS)**, the service profile of the users' current profile, if any. Click **Save**.

## 6. Put MCPTT users on the MC profile

For each MCPTT user:

- Go to the **Subscribers** page and click on the subscriber.
- In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to **Profile**, select the MC profile, and click **Update**.
- Give the subscriber an MSISDN, as in [Enable Voice](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/enable_voice/#3-give-subscribers-an-msisdn), and map its MCPTT public identity, `sip:mcptt-<msisdn>@<IMS home domain>`, to an MCPTT ID on your MCPTT server.
- Program the SIM's ISIM with `sip:mcptt-<msisdn>@<IMS home domain>` in a record of EF.IMPU after the first.

## 7. Verify the MCPTT registration

Start the MCPTT client. Go to the **Subscribers** page and click on the MCPTT user. **MCPTT** should show **Registered**.

## 8. Make an MCPTT call

On the MCPTT client, make a call to another MCPTT user. The call should connect with audio in both directions.

Enable MCPTT in Ella Core

# Enable SMS

This guide connects Ella Core to an SMSC, such as [Ella SMSC](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/smsc/), so subscribers can send and receive SMS.

## 1. Configure the SMSC

In the Ella Core UI, go to **Integrations › SMS**. Under **This Core**, note the **Diameter Realm**, e.g. `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, and each node's **Origin-Host**.

Set your SMSC's HSS realm to the **Diameter Realm**. If your SMSC asks for Ella Core's Origin-Host, enter each node's.

## 2. Connect Ella Core to the SMSC

In **Integrations › SMS**, click the edit icon next to **Serving Node Number**, enter Ella Core's E.164 number for SMS, e.g. `+15550001111`, and click **Update**.

Click **Add SMSC** and configure the following settings:

- **Name**: a name for your SMSC, e.g. `main`.
- **Service Centre Addresses**: the E.164 service centre addresses your SMSC serves, e.g. `+15550000000`.
- **Diameter Peers**: the **Address** of your SMSC's Diameter endpoint. If your SMSC has several Diameter nodes, click **Add Diameter Peer** for each.

Click **Add**.

Validate that each node shows **Connected**.

## 3. Give subscribers an MSISDN

For each subscriber that should send or receive SMS:

- Go to the **Subscribers** page and click on the subscriber you want to configure.
- In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to MSISDN.
- Enter the subscriber's E.164 number, e.g. `+15551230001`, and click on **Update**.

## 4. Set the SMSC number on the phones

On each phone's SIM, set the SMSC number to one of your SMSCs' service centre numbers, in international format, e.g. `+15550000000`.

## 5. Send a test SMS

Send a test SMS message from a phone to another in your private mobile network. The message should be delivered successfully.

Enable SMS in Ella Core

To also deliver SMS over IP through an IMS, see Ella IMS's [Enable SMS over IP](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/enable_sms_over_ip/).

# Enable UE-to-UE communication

Local Switching allows two UEs served by Ella Core to communicate directly with each other.

## Enable local switching

1. Open the Ella Core UI and navigate to **Networking > Data Networks**, then open the data network of the UEs.
1. In **Slices**, toggle **Local switch** to **ON** on the slice of the UEs.

Local switching only connects UEs on the same slice and data network.

The change takes effect on the user plane immediately.

Note

These steps can also be performed via the REST API. See the [Slices API reference](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/api/slices/#update-a-data-network-of-a-slice) for details.

# Enable Voice

This guide lets subscribers in your private mobile network make voice and video calls over 4G and 5G, with an external IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS).

## Prerequisites

- **IMS**: an IMS integrated with Ella Core, as in [Integrate with an IMS](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/integrate_with_ims/index.md).
- **Radio QoS support**: your radios must support the following QoS classes, as QCIs on 4G and 5QIs on 5G.

| QCI / 5QI | Used for       |
| --------- | -------------- |
| 5         | IMS signalling |
| 1         | Voice          |
| 2         | Video          |

## 1. Create the voice data network

Go to the **Networking** page and open the **Data Networks** tab.

Click **Create**, enter `ims` as the **Name**, set the IP pool, turn on **IMS (voice and mission critical services)**, and click **Create**.

Open the `ims` data network, and in **Slices**, select the slice of your subscribers and click **Serve on slice**.

## 2. Add a voice policy to the profiles

For each profile whose subscribers should make calls:

- Go to the **Profiles** page and click on the profile you want to configure.
- Click **Add Policy**, enter a **Name**, set the **Data Network** to `ims`, and click **Create**.

## 3. Give subscribers an MSISDN

For each subscriber that should make or receive calls:

- Go to the **Subscribers** page and click on the subscriber you want to configure.
- In Provisioning, click the edit icon next to MSISDN.
- Enter the subscriber's E.164 number, e.g. `+15551230001`, and click on **Update**.

## 4. Enable voice on the phones

On each phone, turn on VoLTE (4G) or VoNR (5G).

In **Integrations › IMS**, check that **Advertise IMS Voice** is on, the default.

## 5. Verify the IMS registration

Go to the **Subscribers** page and click on a subscriber with an MSISDN. **Voice** should show **Registered**.

## 6. Make a test call

Call a phone from another in your private mobile network. The call should connect with audio in both directions.

Enable Voice in Ella Core

# Install

Ensure your system meets the [requirements](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/system_reqs/index.md). Then, choose one of the installation methods below.

Install the Ella Core snap:

```
sudo snap install ella-core
```

Configure Ella Core:

```
sudo vim /var/snap/ella-core/common/core.yaml
```

Start Ella Core:

```
sudo snap start --enable ella-core.cored
```

Install the required dependencies:

```
sudo snap install go --channel=1.27/stable --classic
sudo snap install node --channel=24/stable --classic
sudo apt update
sudo apt -y install gcc
```

Clone the Ella Core repository:

```
git clone https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git
cd core
```

Build the frontend:

```
npm install --prefix ui
npm run build --prefix ui
```

Build Ella Core:

```
REVISION=`git rev-parse HEAD`
go build -ldflags "-X github.com/ellanetworks/core/version.GitCommit=${REVISION}" ./cmd/core/main.go
```

Configure Ella Core:

```
vim core.yaml
```

Start Ella Core:

```
sudo ./main -config core.yaml
```

Create a new directory:

```
mkdir ella
cd ella
```

Copy the following file into this directory:

docker-compose.yaml

```
configs:
  ella_config:
    content: |
      logging:
        system:
          level: "info"
          output: "stdout"
        audit:
          output: "stdout"
      db:
        path: "/data/ella.db"
      interfaces:
        n2:
          address: "10.3.0.2"
          ngap-port: 38412
        n3:
          name: "n3"
        n6:
          name: "eth0"
        api:
          address: "0.0.0.0"
          port: 5002
      datapath:
        attach-mode: "tcx"

services:
  ella-core:
    image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core:v1.22.0
    configs:
      - source: ella_config
        target: /core.yaml
    restart: unless-stopped
    entrypoint: /bin/core --config /core.yaml
    privileged: true
    volumes:
      - ella-data:/data
    ports:
      - "5002:5002"
    networks:
      default:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: eth0
      n3:
        driver_opts:
          com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname: n3
        ipv4_address: 10.3.0.2

networks:
  n3:
    internal: true
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 10.3.0.0/24

volumes:
  ella-data:
```

Edit the file to match your network interfaces and desired configuration.

Note

This example uses `tcx` mode. To use `xdp-native`, run the container with `network_mode: host` and set `n3` and `n6` to host NICs with native XDP support.

Start the Ella Core container:

```
docker compose up -d
```

Ensure your Kubernetes cluster is running with the [Multus CNI](https://github.com/k8snetworkplumbingwg/multus-cni) installed, and that the `macvlan`, `static`, and `tuning` [CNI plugins](https://github.com/containernetworking/plugins) are present on every node.

Download the Ella Core manifests:

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.22.0 https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git
```

Edit `core/k8s/core-ran-nad.yaml` to set `master` to the host interface that connects to your radios, and set the N2/N3 address.

Deploy Ella Core:

```
kubectl apply -k core/k8s
```

Note

These manifests use `tcx` mode. To use `xdp-native`, move physical N3 and N6 NICs with native XDP support into the pod (e.g. with `host-device`) instead of using macvlan and `eth0`, and put both in a VRF.

# Integrate with an IMS

This guide connects Ella Core to an external IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS), with Ella Core as the IMS's HSS and PCRF. It is the first part of [Enable Voice](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/enable_voice/index.md) and [Enable MCPTT](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/enable_mcptt/index.md). To learn how Ella Core works with the IMS, see [IMS Integration](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/ims_integration/index.md).

This guide uses [Ella IMS](https://github.com/ellanetworks/ims), but any 3GPP-compliant IMS can be used. For the Ella IMS side, see [Integrate with Ella Core](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/ims/how_to/integrate_with_ella_core/).

## 1. Enable the Diameter interface

In the Ella Core configuration file, set the address Ella Core accepts Diameter connections on:

```
interfaces:
  diameter:
    address: "10.3.0.2"
```

In a [high availability cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md), use the same `interfaces.diameter.port` on every node.

Restart Ella Core.

## 2. Configure the IMS

In the Ella Core UI, go to **Integrations › IMS**. Under **This Core**, note the **Diameter Realm**, e.g. `epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, each node's **Origin-Host**, the **Diameter Address**, and the **Home Domain**.

Configure your IMS with the following settings:

- **HSS (Cx)**: Ella Core's **Diameter Address**, e.g. `10.3.0.2`, port `3868`.
- **PCRF (Rx)**: Ella Core's **Diameter Address**, e.g. `10.3.0.2`, port `3868`.
- **HSS and PCRF realm**: Ella Core's **Diameter Realm**, or its **Home Domain**.
- **Home domain**: Ella Core's **Home Domain**, e.g. `ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`.

To use another home domain, e.g. `ims.example.org`, click the edit icon next to **Home Domain**, enter it, click **Update**, then **Confirm**. Set the same home domain on your subscribers' ISIMs.

## 3. Allow your IMS nodes

In **Integrations › IMS**, under **Allowed IMS Peers**, click **Add Allowed Peer** and enter:

- **Name**: e.g. `cscf`.
- **Origin-Host** of an IMS node, e.g. `scscf.ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, or the **Realm** of your IMS nodes, e.g. `ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org`, or both.
- **Source Addresses**: the IP addresses or CIDR prefixes your IMS nodes connect from, e.g. `10.3.0.0/24`. At least one is required.

Click **Add**. Repeat for each group of IMS nodes: I-CSCF, S-CSCF, P-CSCF and application servers.

## 4. Restrict Diameter access to your IMS nodes

In **Integrations › IMS**, under **This Core**, click the edit icon next to **Restrict to Allowed Peers**, turn it on, and click **Update**.

## 5. Set the P-CSCF addresses

In **Integrations › IMS**, click the edit icon next to **P-CSCF Addresses**, enter your IMS's P-CSCF addresses or host names, e.g. `10.6.0.5`, and click **Update**.

## 6. Route the IMS data networks

In your IMS, add a route to the IP pools of your IMS data networks via Ella Core's N6 address, with an MTU of 1400, e.g. `ip route add 10.0.0.0/8 via 10.6.0.2 mtu lock 1400`.

# Integrate with a Radio

Radios are automatically added to Ella Core as they connect to the network as long as they are configured to use the same Operator information as Ella Core.

Follow this guide to integrate Ella Core with a radio. This guide assumes you have already deployed Ella Core.

## 1. Configure the Operator information

1. Open Ella Core in your web browser.
1. Click on the **Operator** tab in the left-hand menu.
1. Edit the Operator information:
   - **MCC**: The Mobile Country Code for the operator.
   - **MNC**: The Mobile Network Code for the operator.
   - **Supported TACs**: A list of supported Tracking Area Codes (TACs).

## 2. Configure the radio

In your radio's configuration, you will likely need to specify the following information to connect it with a mobile core network:

- **AMF / MME Address**: The address of the N2 / S1-MME interface on Ella Core.
- **PLMN ID**: The Public Land Mobile Network Identifier. This is a combination of the Mobile Country Code (MCC) and the Mobile Network Code (MNC). You can find this information in Ella Core under **Operator** and **Operator ID**.
- **TAC**: The Tracking Area Code. You can find this information in Ella Core under **Operator** and **Supported TACs**.
- **SST (5G only)**: The Slice/Service Type. Identifies a network slice. You can find this information in Ella Core under **Networking** and **Slices**.
- **SD (5G only)**: The Slice Differentiator. Optionally differentiates slices sharing the same SST. You can find this information in Ella Core under **Networking** and **Slices**.

Note

Each radio has its own configuration interface. Consult the radio's documentation for specific instructions.

# Use native XDP with veth interfaces

When Ella Core's N3 or N6 interface is a veth pair and XDP is set to `native` mode, the peer side of the veth must have an XDP program attached, or traffic redirected out of that interface fails. This guide attaches a minimal one.

For an explanation of why this is needed, see [XDP redirect on veth pairs](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/user_plane_packet_processing_with_ebpf/#xdp-redirect-on-veth-pairs).

## 1. Install prerequisites

Install the BPF toolchain needed to compile the XDP program:

```
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y clang llvm libbpf-dev linux-headers-$(uname -r)
```

## 2. Create the zero entrypoint program

Create a file called `zero_entrypoint.c` with the following content:

```
#include <linux/bpf.h>
#include <bpf/bpf_helpers.h>

SEC("xdp")
int zero_entrypoint(struct xdp_md *ctx)
{
    return XDP_PASS;
}

char _license[] SEC("license") = "GPL";
```

## 3. Compile the program

```
clang -O2 -g -Wall -target bpf -c zero_entrypoint.c -o zero_entrypoint.o
```

## 4. Attach the program to the peer veth

Attach the compiled program to the peer veth interface. If the peer is in a network namespace (e.g. `n3ns`), use `ip netns exec`:

```
sudo ip netns exec n3ns ip link set dev n3-ran-veth xdpgeneric off
sudo ip netns exec n3ns ip link set dev n3-ran-veth xdp obj zero_entrypoint.o sec xdp
```

If the peer is not in a namespace:

```
sudo ip link set dev <peer-veth-name> xdp obj zero_entrypoint.o sec xdp
```

## 5. Verify

Confirm the program is attached:

```
sudo ip netns exec n3ns ip link show n3-ran-veth
```

You should see `prog/xdp` in the output.

## 6. Configure Ella Core for native XDP

Set the attach mode to `xdp-native` in the Ella Core configuration file:

```
datapath:
  attach-mode: "xdp-native"
```

Restart Ella Core for the change to take effect.

This guide describes the steps and settings required to tune network performance for Ella Core. It was written with 10Gbps NICs in mind. The exact values required will depend on the hardware used.

## Configure transmit queue length

Increase the transmit queue length to 10000 by adding the following line to `/etc/udev/rules.d/60-ella-core.rules` for each interfaces handling N3 or N6 traffic:

```
KERNEL=="enp4s0f0", RUN+="/sbin/ip link set %k txqueuelen 10000"
```

## Configure multiqueue

For all interfaces handling N3 or N6 traffic, configure multiple queues. The appropriate number of queues is the larger between the number of cores and the maximum number of queues supported by the NIC:

```
nic=enp4s0f0
nproc=$(nproc)
max_allowed=$(sudo ethtool -l $nic | grep Combined | awk '{ print $2 }' | sort -n | head -n 1)
if [ $nproc -ge $max_allowed ]; then
    echo $nproc
else
    echo $max_allowed
fi
```

Assuming the above script output was 16, add the following line to `/etc/udev/rules.d/60-ella-core.rules`:

```
KERNEL=="enp4s0f0", RUN+="/usr/sbin/ethtool -L %k combined 16"
```

## Increase the NIC ring buffer sizes

Find the maximum allowed ring buffer sizes allowed by your hardware:

```
sudo ethtool -g enp4s0f0
```

The output should be similar to this:

```
Ring parameters for enp4s0f0:
Pre-set maximums:
RX:         8192
RX Mini:        n/a
RX Jumbo:       n/a
TX:         8192
TX push buff len:   n/a
Current hardware settings:
RX:         512
RX Mini:        n/a
RX Jumbo:       n/a
TX:         512
RX Buf Len:     n/a
CQE Size:       n/a
TX Push:        off
RX Push:        off
TX push buff len:   n/a
TCP data split:     n/a
```

Add the following line to `/etc/udev/rules.d/60-ella-core.rules`, using the values from the `Pre-set maximums` section:

```
KERNEL=="enp4s0f0", RUN+="/usr/sbin/ethtool -G %k rx 8192 tx 8192"
```

## Tune maximum backlog in the receive queues

Increase the maximum backlog in receive queues by adding the following content to `/etc/sysctl.d/99-ella-core.conf`:

```
# increase the maximum backlog
net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 182757
```

## Apply the changes

The changes in this guide can be applied by either rebooting, or running the following commands:

```
sudo udevadm trigger
sudo sysctl --system
```

# Scale Up a High Availability Cluster

This guide walks through adding a node to an existing Ella Core high-availability cluster.

## Prerequisites

- A running HA cluster deployed (see [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md)).
- A prepared host with Ella Core installed per the [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/install/index.md) guide with `cluster.bind-address` set in the configuration file.

## Add a node

1. Open the **Cluster** page on any node in the cluster.
1. Click **Add Node**, click **Mint Token**, and copy the token.
1. Start Ella Core on the new host.
1. Open the new node's UI in a browser. Click on **Join an existing cluster instead**, paste the token, enter the cluster address of a node already in the cluster, and click **Join**.
1. On the **Cluster** page, verify the new node appears and is shown as **Healthy**.

# Upgrade

## Prerequisites

- Ella Core installed with [Install](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/install/index.md) or [Deploy a High Availability Cluster](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/deploy_ha_cluster/index.md).
- The target release is the next minor release after the running one.

## 1. Review the release notes

Read the [release notes](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/reference/releases/index.md) of the target release. Apply any action listed under **Breaking changes**.

## 2. Back up

Create a backup with [Backup and Restore](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/backup_and_restore/#backup).

## 3. Upgrade

```
sudo snap refresh ella-core
```

In `docker-compose.yaml`, set the image tag to the target release:

```
image: ghcr.io/ellanetworks/ella-core:<target-version>
```

Recreate the container:

```
docker compose up -d
```

Download the manifests of the target release:

```
git clone --depth 1 --branch <target-version> https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git core-<target-version>
```

Reapply your changes to `core-<target-version>/k8s/core-ran-nad.yaml` and `core-<target-version>/k8s/core-configmap.yaml`.

Apply the manifests:

```
kubectl apply -k core-<target-version>/k8s
```

Wait for the rollout to complete:

```
kubectl -n ella rollout status statefulset/ella-core
```

Upgrade the followers first and the leader last. Repeat these steps for each node:

1. Open the **Cluster** page on any healthy node other than the one you are about to upgrade.

1. Click **Drain** next to the node. Wait until its **Drain State** is `drained`.

1. On that host, refresh the snap:

   ```
   sudo snap refresh ella-core
   ```

1. On the **Cluster** page, wait for the node to return to **Healthy**.

1. Click **Resume** next to the node. Wait until its **Drain State** is `active`.

## 4. Verify

```
curl -k <ella-core-api-url>/api/v1/status
```

Confirm `version` is the target release and `ready` is `true`.

On the **Cluster** page, confirm:

- Every node's **Version** is the target release.
- Every node is **Healthy** and its **Drain State** is `active`.
- **Schema** shows a single version.

## Roll back

1. Stop Ella Core:

   ```
   sudo snap stop --disable ella-core.cored
   ```

1. Revert to the previous release:

   ```
   sudo snap revert ella-core
   ```

1. Restore the backup with [Offline Restore](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/backup_and_restore/#offline-restore-disaster-recovery).

1. In `docker-compose.yaml`, set the image tag back to the previous release.

1. Stop the container:

   ```
   docker compose stop
   ```

1. Delete the database from the data volume:

   ```
   docker run --rm -v <project>_ella-data:/data alpine sh -c 'rm -rf /data/ella.db /data/ella.db-wal /data/ella.db-shm /data/raft /data/cluster-tls'
   ```

1. Copy the backup into the data volume as `restore.bundle`:

   ```
   docker compose cp backup.tar.gz ella-core:/data/restore.bundle
   ```

1. Recreate the container:

   ```
   docker compose up -d
   ```

1. Scale Ella Core down:

   ```
   kubectl -n ella scale statefulset/ella-core --replicas=0
   ```

1. Start a pod that mounts the data volume:

   ```
   kubectl -n ella run restore --image=alpine --restart=Never \
     --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"restore","image":"alpine","command":["sleep","3600"],"volumeMounts":[{"name":"data","mountPath":"/data"}]}],"volumes":[{"name":"data","persistentVolumeClaim":{"claimName":"data-ella-core-0"}}]}}'
   kubectl -n ella wait --for=condition=Ready pod/restore
   ```

1. Delete the database and copy the backup as `restore.bundle`:

   ```
   kubectl -n ella exec restore -- sh -c 'rm -rf /data/ella.db /data/ella.db-wal /data/ella.db-shm /data/raft /data/cluster-tls'
   kubectl -n ella cp backup.tar.gz restore:/data/restore.bundle
   kubectl -n ella delete pod restore
   ```

1. Download the manifests of the previous release:

   ```
   git clone --depth 1 --branch <previous-version> https://github.com/ellanetworks/core.git core-<previous-version>
   ```

1. Reapply your changes to `core-<previous-version>/k8s/core-ran-nad.yaml` and `core-<previous-version>/k8s/core-configmap.yaml`.

1. Apply the manifests:

   ```
   kubectl apply -k core-<previous-version>/k8s
   ```

1. Scale Ella Core up:

   ```
   kubectl -n ella scale statefulset/ella-core --replicas=1
   ```

1. On every node, stop Ella Core and revert to the previous release:

   ```
   sudo snap stop --disable ella-core.cored
   sudo snap revert ella-core
   ```

1. Restore the backup with [Offline Restore](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/how_to/backup_and_restore/#offline-restore-disaster-recovery).

Any interface used by Ella Core can be on a VLAN interface. First, configure the VLAN on the host system, then use the name of the VLAN interface in the configuration file:

```
logging:
  system:
    level: "info"
    output: "stdout"
  audit:
    output: "stdout"
db:
  path: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/data/ella.db"
interfaces:
  n2:
    address: "10.3.0.2"
    ngap-port: 38412
  n3:
    name: "ens5.103"
  n6:
    name: "ens3.106"
  api:
    address: "0.0.0.0"
    port: 5002
    tls:
      cert: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/cert.pem"
      key: "/var/snap/ella-core/common/key.pem"
datapath:
  attach-mode: "xdp-native"
telemetry:
  enabled: false
```

Any interface used by Ella Core can be in a VRF.

## Use netplan to configure N3 and N6 in a user-plane VRF

Edit your netplan configuration:

```
network:
  vrfs:
    up-vrf:
      table: 1001
      interfaces:
        - enp4s0f0
        - enp4s0f1
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.6.0.1
          metric: 100
        # High metric unreachable route to prevent lookups in other tables
        - to: 0.0.0.0/0
          type: unreachable
          metric: 9000
  ethernets:
    enp2s0:
      addresses:
        - 10.1.0.10/24
      nameservers:
        addresses:
          - 1.1.1.1
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.1.0.1
    enp4s0f0:
      addresses:
        - 10.6.0.3/24
    enp4s0f1:
      addresses:
        - 10.3.0.3/24

  version: 2
```

N3 and N6 must share a VRF

The N3 and N6 interfaces must be assigned to the **same** VRF. Ella Core will refuse to start otherwise.

## Configure Ella Core

Use the interfaces directly in the configuration file:

```
interfaces:
  n2:
    address: "10.1.0.10"
  n3:
    name: "enp4s0f1"
  n6:
    name: "enp4s0f0"
  api:
    address: "10.1.0.10"
    port: 5002
```
