```
                            "state": "down",
                            "since": "2026-09-29T13:44:09Z",
                            "error": "dial 192.0.2.11:3868: connection refused"
                        }
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Get an SMSC

This path returns an SMSC.

| Method | Path                                    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/sms/smscs/{name}` |

### Parameters

None

## Create an SMSC

This path creates an SMSC.

| Method | Path                             |
| ------ | -------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/integrations/sms/smscs` |

### Parameters

- `name` (string): The name of the SMSC.
- `serviceCentres` (array of strings): The E.164 service centre numbers the SMSC serves, for example `+15550000000`.
- `nodes` (array of objects): The SMSC's Diameter nodes.
  - `originHost` (optional string): The node's Origin-Host. When set, the node must give this Origin-Host when it connects.
  - `address` (string): The IPv4 or IPv6 address or the host name of the node's Diameter endpoint.
  - `port` (optional integer): The SCTP port of the node's Diameter endpoint, between 1 and 65535. Defaults to `3868`.

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "main",
    "serviceCentres": ["+15550000000"],
    "nodes": [
        {
            "originHost": "smsc1.node.example.org",
            "address": "192.0.2.10"
        },
        {
            "originHost": "smsc2.node.example.org",
            "address": "192.0.2.11"
        }
    ]
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "name": "main",
        "serviceCentres": ["+15550000000"],
        "nodes": [
            {
                "originHost": "smsc1.node.example.org",
                "address": "192.0.2.10",
                "port": 3868
            },
            {
                "originHost": "smsc2.node.example.org",
                "address": "192.0.2.11",
                "port": 3868
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Update an SMSC

This path updates an SMSC.

| Method | Path                                    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/integrations/sms/smscs/{name}` |

### Parameters

Same as [Create an SMSC](#create-an-smsc), without `name`.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "SMSC updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Delete an SMSC

This path deletes an SMSC.

| Method | Path                                    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/integrations/sms/smscs/{name}` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "SMSC deleted successfully"
    }
}
```

## Get the IMS Settings

This path returns the P-CSCF addresses, the voice status, the IMS home domain, whether IMS voice is advertised, and whether peers are restricted to the allowed IMS peers.

| Method | Path                       |
| ------ | -------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "pcscfAddresses": ["192.0.2.20", "2001:db8::20"],
        "voiceStatus": "enabled",
        "homeDomain": "ims.example.org",
        "derivedHomeDomain": "ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "advertiseVoice": true,
        "restrictPeers": true
    }
}
```

| Field            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `voiceStatus`    | Whether the IMS configuration is ready for voice: `enabled`, `no_pcscf`, `no_ims_data_network` (no IMS data network named `ims`), or `ip_family_mismatch` (no P-CSCF address shares an IP version with the pools of the `ims` data network). |
| `homeDomain`     | The configured IMS home domain. Empty when `derivedHomeDomain` is used.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `advertiseVoice` | `true` when Ella Core tells home UEs that IMS voice is supported.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `restrictPeers`  | `true` when only peers matching an [allowed IMS peer](#create-an-allowed-ims-peer) may connect.                                                                                                                                              |

## Update the IMS Settings

This path sets the P-CSCF addresses, the IMS home domain, whether IMS voice is advertised, and whether peers are restricted to the allowed IMS peers. Changing the home domain moves the identities of the IMS application servers to the new domain and de-registers the subscribers whose public identities change.

| Method | Path                       |
| ------ | -------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims` |

### Parameters

- `pcscfAddresses` (array of strings): Unicast IPv4 and IPv6 addresses or host names of the IMS, in preference order. At most 10, with at most 5 addresses of each IP version, without duplicates. UEs receive the addresses of the IP version they request. An empty list clears it. A changed list applies to new IMS sessions.
- `homeDomain` (string): The IMS home domain, a domain name with at least two labels. An empty string, or the derived domain itself, uses the domain derived from the operator ID, `ims.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`. The EPC realm and `3gppnetwork.org` domains of other PLMNs are rejected. Ella Core accepts Diameter requests addressed to it.
- `advertiseVoice` (boolean): Whether Ella Core tells every home UE that IMS voice is supported. It applies at each UE's next registration, attach or tracking area update. Roamers are never told.
- `restrictPeers` (boolean): Whether only peers matching an [allowed IMS peer](#create-an-allowed-ims-peer) may connect. With no allowed IMS peer, every peer is rejected. Turning it on disconnects connected peers that match none.

All four are required.

### Sample Request

```
{
    "pcscfAddresses": ["pcscf.ims.example.org", "192.0.2.20", "2001:db8::20"],
    "homeDomain": "ims.example.org",
    "advertiseVoice": true,
    "restrictPeers": true
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "IMS settings updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## List Allowed IMS Peers

This path returns the allowed IMS peers, each with this node's connections from the peers it matches.

| Method | Path                                     |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/allowed-peers` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "name": "cscf",
                "realm": "ims.example.org",
                "addresses": ["10.3.0.0/24", "2001:db8:3::/64"],
                "connections": [
                    {
                        "state": "open",
                        "originHost": "scscf.ims.example.org",
                        "realm": "ims.example.org",
                        "since": "2026-10-05T13:44:09Z"
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Get an Allowed IMS Peer

This path returns an allowed IMS peer.

| Method | Path                                            |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/allowed-peers/{name}` |

### Parameters

None

## Create an Allowed IMS Peer

This path creates an allowed IMS peer. At most 32 allowed IMS peers can be configured.

| Method | Path                                     |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/allowed-peers` |

### Parameters

- `name` (string): The name of the allowed IMS peer.
- `originHost` (optional string): The Origin-Host the peer must give, a fully qualified domain name, compared case-insensitively.
- `realm` (optional string): The Origin-Realm the peer must give, a fully qualified domain name.
- `addresses` (array of strings): The IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or CIDR prefixes the peer connects from, at least one and at most 16, e.g. `10.3.0.5` or `10.3.0.0/24`. A bare address means a `/32` or `/128` prefix. `0.0.0.0/0` and `::/0` allow any source address. They are returned as canonical prefixes, sorted and without duplicates.

At least one of `originHost` and `realm` is required.

A Diameter peer matches an allowed IMS peer when it connects from one of the `addresses` and gives the `originHost` and `realm` that are set. Matching peers are labelled `ims`. When `restrictPeers` is set in the [IMS settings](#update-the-ims-settings), other peers are rejected.

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "cscf",
    "realm": "ims.example.org",
    "addresses": ["10.3.0.0/24", "2001:db8:3::/64"]
}
```

### Responses

| Status | Condition                                                                                     |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `201`  | Returns the created allowed IMS peer.                                                         |
| `400`  | Invalid parameters.                                                                           |
| `409`  | The name is taken, or another allowed IMS peer has the same Origin-Host, realm and addresses. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "name": "cscf",
        "realm": "ims.example.org",
        "addresses": ["10.3.0.0/24", "2001:db8:3::/64"],
        "connections": []
    }
}
```

## Update an Allowed IMS Peer

| Method | Path                                            |

| PUT    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/allowed-peers/{name}` |

### Parameters

Same as [Create an Allowed IMS Peer](#create-an-allowed-ims-peer), without `name`.

```

        "message": "Allowed IMS peer updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Get an IMS Application Server

This path returns an IMS application server.

| Method | Path                                                  |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/application-servers/{name}` |

### Parameters

None

## Create an IMS Application Server

This path creates an IMS application server.

| Method | Path                                           |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/application-servers` |

### Parameters

- `name` (string): The name of the application server.
- `serverName` (string): The SIP URI of the application server.
- `publicServiceIdentities` (optional array of strings): The SIP or tel URIs the application server hosts. A wildcarded identity uses the `!regex!` syntax, for example `sip:!.*!@mcptt.ims.example.org`. Identities are stored in canonical form: lowercase scheme and host, no URI parameters, and tel numbers without visual separators. An identity can't be hosted by, or overlap one of, another application server, be or cover a subscriber's public identity (`sip:+<msisdn>@<IMS home domain>`, `tel:+<msisdn>` or `sip:mcptt-<msisdn>@<IMS home domain>`), or take the form of a subscriber identity (`sip:<IMSI>@<IMS home domain>`).

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "mcptt",
    "serverName": "sip:mcptt.ims.example.org",
    "publicServiceIdentities": ["sip:!.*!@mcptt.ims.example.org"]
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "name": "mcptt",
        "serverName": "sip:mcptt.ims.example.org",
        "publicServiceIdentities": ["sip:!.*!@mcptt.ims.example.org"]
    }
}
```

## Update an IMS Application Server

| Method | Path                                                  |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/application-servers/{name}` |

### Parameters

Same as [Create an IMS Application Server](#create-an-ims-application-server), without `name`.

### Sample Response

```
    "result": {
        "message": "Application server updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Get an IMS Service Profile

| Method | Path                                               |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/service-profiles/{name}` |

### Parameters

None

## Create an IMS Service Profile

This path creates an IMS service profile.

| Method | Path                                        |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/service-profiles` |

### Parameters

- `name` (string): The name of the service profile.
- `initialFilterCriteria` (optional array): In priority order ([TS 29.228 Annex B.2.2](https://www.3gpp.org/DynaReport/29228.htm)). Each criterion has:
  - `applicationServerName` (string): The name of the [IMS application server](#create-an-ims-application-server) matching requests are sent to.
  - `trigger` (optional object): Without it, the criterion matches every request.
    - `conditionsMatch` (string): `all` if a group matches when all of its conditions match, and the trigger matches when any group matches. `any` if a group matches when any of its conditions matches, and the trigger matches when every group matches.
    - `groups` (array): Groups of `conditions`. Each condition has an optional `negated` (boolean) and exactly one of `requestURI` (string), `method` (string), `sipHeader` (`{header, content}`), `sessionCase` (`ORIGINATING_REGISTERED`, `TERMINATING_REGISTERED`, `TERMINATING_UNREGISTERED`, `ORIGINATING_UNREGISTERED` or `ORIGINATING_CDIV`) and `sessionDescription` (`{line, content}`). With the `REGISTER` method, `registrationTypes` lists up to two of `INITIAL_REGISTRATION`, `RE-REGISTRATION` and `DE-REGISTRATION`. Request URIs, headers, lines and contents are extended regular expressions.
  - `profilePart` (optional string): `REGISTERED` or `UNREGISTERED`, the part of the user profile the criterion belongs to. Omitted for both.
  - `defaultHandling` (optional string): `SESSION_CONTINUED` or `SESSION_TERMINATED`, what the S-CSCF does when the application server can't be reached.
  - `serviceInfo` (optional string): Passed transparently to the application server.
  - `includeRegisterRequest` (optional boolean)
  - `includeRegisterResponse` (optional boolean)

The `priority` of a criterion is its position in the list. It is returned on reads and ignored on writes.

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "conference",
    "initialFilterCriteria": [
        {
            "applicationServerName": "conference",
            "trigger": {
                "conditionsMatch": "all",
                "groups": [{"conditions": [{"requestURI": "^sip:conference@.*$"}]}]
            },
            "defaultHandling": "SESSION_TERMINATED"
        }
    ]
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "name": "conference",
        "initialFilterCriteria": [
            {
                "priority": 0,
                "applicationServerName": "conference",
                "trigger": {
                    "conditionsMatch": "all",
                    "groups": [{"conditions": [{"requestURI": "^sip:conference@.*$"}]}]
                },
                "defaultHandling": "SESSION_TERMINATED",
                "includeRegisterRequest": false,
                "includeRegisterResponse": false
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Update an IMS Service Profile

This path replaces the initial filter criteria of an IMS service profile. Registered subscribers whose profile assigns it get the new user profile.

| Method | Path                                               |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/integrations/ims/service-profiles/{name}` |

### Parameters

- `initialFilterCriteria` (array): In priority order, as in [Create an IMS Service Profile](#create-an-ims-service-profile). An empty list removes all of them.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Service profile updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## List Roaming Partners

This path returns the list of roaming partners. For a partner with a 5G agreement, `n32` gives the N32-c context of this node, when it has `interfaces.n32`.

| Method | Path                                    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/partners` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "0199a3c2-1f4e-7d21-8c9b-5a6e7f8091a2",
                "name": "Partner Telecom",
                "plmns": [
                    {"mcc": "999", "mnc": "70"}
                ],
                "profileName": "roamers",
                "sepp": {
                    "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org",
                    "n32cURI": "https://sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org:443",
                    "trustAnchorPEM": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
                },
                "diameterPeerID": "0199a3c2-5c1e-7b8e-9f3a-2d4c6e8f0a1b",
                "n32": {
                    "state": "established"
                }
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

| N32 field   | Description                                                                                    |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `state`     | `idle`, `establishing`, `established`, `failed`, or `unknown` (the handshake could not start). |
| `peer`      | The partner SEPP the context is with, when the handshake was redirected.                       |
| `lastError` | The reason of the last failure.                                                                |

## Create a Roaming Partner

This path creates a new roaming partner.

| Method | Path                                    |
| ------ | --------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/partners` |

### Parameters

- `name` (string): The name of the partner. Must be unique.
- `plmns` (array): The partner's PLMN IDs, at least one.
  - `mcc` (string): 3 digits.
  - `mnc` (string): 2 or 3 digits.
  - `nrfAPIRoot` (string, optional): The apiRoot (`http` or `https`) of the NRF of this PLMN, for its roamers. Defaults to `https://nrf.5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org` of this PLMN ID. Needs `sepp`.
- `profileName` (string): The name of the profile applied to the partner's roamers.
- `sepp` (object, optional): The 5G agreement.
  - `fqdn` (string): The partner SEPP's FQDN, as in its certificate: `<host>.5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`, or `<host>.5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.<IPX ID>.ipxnetwork.org`, for one of the partner's PLMN IDs.
  - `n32cURI` (string): The apiRoot of the partner SEPP's N32-c endpoint: `https`, host, optional port and optional path prefix.
  - `n32fURI` (string, optional): The apiRoot of the partner SEPP's N32-f endpoint. Defaults to `n32cURI`.
  - `trustAnchorPEM` (string): The CA certificates that the partner SEPP's certificate chains to, or the partner's self-signed certificate, in PEM. Each certificate must be valid, with an ECDSA key or an RSA key of at least 2048 bits.
- `diameterPeerID` (string, optional): The ID of the [roaming Diameter peer](#create-a-roaming-diameter-peer) of the 4G agreement.

### Sample Request

```
{
    "name": "Partner Telecom",
    "plmns": [{"mcc": "999", "mnc": "70"}],
    "profileName": "roamers",
    "sepp": {
        "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org",
        "n32cURI": "https://sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org:443",
        "trustAnchorPEM": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
    },
    "diameterPeerID": "0199a3c2-5c1e-7b8e-9f3a-2d4c6e8f0a1b"
}
```

### Responses

| Status | Condition                                                |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `201`  | Returns the created partner.                             |
| `400`  | Invalid parameters.                                      |
| `404`  | The profile or the roaming Diameter peer does not exist. |
| `409`  | The name is taken, or a PLMN ID conflicts.               |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": "0199a3c2-1f4e-7d21-8c9b-5a6e7f8091a2",
        "name": "Partner Telecom",
        "plmns": [
            {"mcc": "999", "mnc": "70"}
        ],
        "profileName": "roamers",
        "sepp": {
            "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org",
            "n32cURI": "https://sepp1.5gc.mnc070.mcc999.3gppnetwork.org:443",
            "trustAnchorPEM": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n"
        },
        "diameterPeerID": "0199a3c2-5c1e-7b8e-9f3a-2d4c6e8f0a1b"
    }
}
```

## Update a Roaming Partner

This path updates an existing roaming partner. When a removed PLMN ID or agreement still has roamers, all the partner's roamers are first deregistered on every node, and purged at their home network.

| Method | Path                                         |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/partners/{id}` |

### Parameters

The parameters of [Create a Roaming Partner](#create-a-roaming-partner).

### Responses

| Status | Condition                                                                                                               |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `200`  | The partner is updated.                                                                                                 |
| `400`  | Invalid parameters.                                                                                                     |
| `404`  | The partner, the profile or the roaming Diameter peer does not exist.                                                   |
| `409`  | The name is taken, a PLMN ID conflicts, or the roamers were not all deregistered within one minute. Nothing is changed. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Roaming partner updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Delete a Roaming Partner

This path deletes a roaming partner. Its roamers are first deregistered on every node, and purged at their home network. The usage of its roamers is kept.

| `404`  | The partner does not exist.                                                  |

```

        "message": "Roaming partner deleted successfully"
```

## Re-run the N32 Handshake

This path starts a new N32-c handshake with the partner's SEPP on this node. It returns the state right after the start.

| Method | Path                                                   |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| POST   | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/partners/{id}/handshake` |

### Parameters

None

### Responses

| Status | Condition                                                              |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `202`  | The handshake started.                                                 |
| `404`  | The partner does not exist.                                            |
| `409`  | The partner has no 5G agreement, or this node has no `interfaces.n32`. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "n32": {
            "state": "establishing"
        }
    }
}
```

## Get the SEPP Status

This path returns the N32 listener and SEPP ID of this node, the stored certificate of each SEPP ID, and the trust anchors to give roaming partners.

| Method | Path                                |
| ------ | ----------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/sepp` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "listener": {
            "seppID": 1,
            "configured": true,
            "address": "192.0.2.11",
            "port": 443,
            "listening": true
        },
        "certificates": [
            {
                "seppID": 1,
                "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "source": "generated",
                "subject": "CN=sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org,O=5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "sans": ["sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
                "issuer": "CN=SEPP CA,O=5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "notBefore": "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z",
                "notAfter": "2029-10-01T08:00:00Z",
                "fingerprint": "sha256:a1b2...7e",
                "trustAnchorFingerprint": "sha256:5f0c...9a"
            }
        ],
        "trustAnchors": [
            {
                "source": "generated",
                "subject": "CN=SEPP CA,O=5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "fingerprint": "sha256:5f0c...9a",
                "notAfter": "2036-10-01T08:00:00Z",
                "pem": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n",
                "seppIDs": [1, 2]
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

`seppIDs` lists the nodes that use each trust anchor.

## Import a SEPP Certificate

This path replaces a node's SEPP certificate with one issued by your CA. When the FQDN or the trust anchor changes, the node runs the N32 handshake again with every partner.

| Method | Path                                                           |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/sepp/nodes/{seppID}/certificate` |

### Parameters

- `certificateChainPEM` (string): The certificate, then any intermediates, ending with the CA certificate that partners trust. The certificate must be an end-entity certificate with keyUsage digitalSignature, extendedKeyUsage serverAuth and clientAuth (or none), and a subjectAltName DNS name under `5gc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org` of your PLMN ID.
- `privateKeyPEM` (string): The certificate's private key: ECDSA P-256 or P-384, or RSA of at least 2048 bits.
- `fqdn` (string, optional): The node's SEPP FQDN, when the certificate has several DNS names. Defaults to the subject CN.

### Responses

| Status | Condition                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `200`  | Returns the imported certificate, as listed in [Get the SEPP Status](#get-the-sepp-status), with `warnings`: a missing extendedKeyUsage, a validity over 3 years, or a trust anchor that partners must import. |
| `400`  | Invalid certificate or key.                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `409`  | Another node has this FQDN.                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "seppID": 1,
        "fqdn": "sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "source": "imported",
        "subject": "CN=sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "sans": ["sepp1.5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org"],
        "issuer": "CN=Operator Root CA",
        "notBefore": "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z",
        "notAfter": "2028-10-01T08:00:00Z",
        "fingerprint": "sha256:d4e5...01",
        "trustAnchorFingerprint": "sha256:77aa...3c",
        "warnings": [
            "The trust anchor of this node changed: every roaming partner must import the new trust anchor before N32 with this node works again"
        ]
    }
}
```

## Delete a SEPP Certificate

This path deletes a node's SEPP certificate, generated or imported. The node then generates a new one signed by the cluster SEPP CA. Use it to return to a generated certificate after an import.

| Method | Path                                                           |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/sepp/nodes/{seppID}/certificate` |

### Parameters

None

### Responses

| Status | Condition                         |
| ------ | --------------------------------- |
| `200`  | The certificate was deleted.      |
| `400`  | `seppID` is not between 1 and 63. |
| `404`  | The node has no SEPP certificate. |

## Regenerate the SEPP CA

This path replaces the cluster SEPP CA and deletes every generated SEPP certificate; each node then generates a new one with the new CA. Imported certificates are kept.

| Method | Path                                              |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/integrations/roaming/sepp/ca/regenerate` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "trustAnchor": {
            "source": "generated",
            "subject": "CN=SEPP CA,O=5gc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
            "fingerprint": "sha256:c47d...12",
            "notAfter": "2036-11-03T10:00:00Z",
            "pem": "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----\n",
            "seppIDs": []
        },
        "warnings": [
            "The cluster SEPP CA changed: every roaming partner must import the new trust anchor before N32 with the nodes that use generated certificates works again"
        ]
    }
}
```

## Get the Diameter Status

This path returns Ella Core's Diameter realm, the Origin-Host of every cluster node, the Diameter listener, and the state of this node's Diameter peers.

| Method | Path                            |
| ------ | ------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/integrations/diameter` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "realm": "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
        "servedRealms": [
            "epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
            "ims.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
            "ims.example.org"
        ],
        "nodes": [
            {
                "nodeId": "1",
                "displayName": "core-1",
                "originHost": "mmec01.mmegi0001.mme.epc.mnc001.mcc001.3gppnetwork.org",
                "local": true
            }
        ],
        "listener": {
            "enabled": true,
            "addresses": ["192.0.2.1"],
            "port": 3868
        },
        "peers": [
            {
                "id": "smsc-0199a3c2-7a10-7c3e-8d2f-4b5c6d7e8f90",
                "role": "smsc",
                "owner": {
                    "kind": "smsc",
                    "name": "main"
                },
                "originHost": "smsc.example.org",
                "realm": "example.org",
                "address": "192.0.2.10",
                "port": 3868,
                "direction": "outbound",
                "state": "open",
                "since": "2026-09-29T13:44:09Z"
            },
            {
                "id": "scscf.ims.example.org",
                "role": "ims",
                "owner": {
                    "kind": "imsPeer",
                    "name": "cscf"
                },
                "originHost": "scscf.ims.example.org",
                "realm": "ims.example.org",
                "address": "192.0.2.20",
                "direction": "inbound",
                "state": "open",
                "since": "2026-10-05T13:44:09Z"
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

| Field               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `realm`             | Ella Core's Diameter realm, `epc.mnc<MNC>.mcc<MCC>.3gppnetwork.org`.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `servedRealms`      | The realms Ella Core accepts requests for: `realm`, the derived IMS home domain, and the configured IMS home domain.                                                                                                                                            |
| `peers[].role`      | `smsc` for an [SMSC](#list-smscs) node, `ims` for a peer that matches an [allowed IMS peer](#list-allowed-ims-peers), `roaming` for a [roaming Diameter peer](#list-roaming-diameter-peers), or `unknown` for an inbound peer that matches no allowed IMS peer. |
| `peers[].owner`     | The SMSC, allowed IMS peer, or roaming Diameter peer of the connection: `kind` is `smsc`, `imsPeer`, or `roamingDiameterPeer`; `name` is its name, or its ID for a roaming Diameter peer.                                                                       |
| `peers[].direction` | `inbound` when the peer connects to Ella Core, `outbound` when Ella Core connects to the peer. Inbound peers have no `port`.                                                                                                                                    |
| `peers[].error`     | The reason the last connection failed, when the peer is not connected.                                                                                                                                                                                          |

# Location (beta)

Ella Core supports three positioning methods: Cell ID, Enhanced Cell ID (E-CID), and GNSS in standalone mode. The Location API requests a subscriber's location, manages periodic location requests, and provisions the cell positions those estimates are drawn from.

Beta

The Location API is experimental and served under `/api/beta`. Its paths and payloads may change without notice.

## Locate a Subscriber

This path returns a subscriber's current location.

| Method | Path                 |
| ------ | -------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/beta/location` |

### Parameters

- `supi` (string): Subscriber identity.
- `method` (string, optional): `cell_id`, `ecid`, or `gnss`. Defaults to `cell_id`.
- `mode` (string, optional): `network_based` or `ue_assisted` for `ecid`; `standalone` for `gnss`. Defaults to every mode supported by `method`.
- `measurement_quantities` (object, optional): E-CID measurement quantities (TS 38.455, TS 36.455). Only for `ecid` with `mode` `network_based` or omitted.
  - `nr` (array of strings, optional): Used when the serving cell is NR. Each entry must be one of `cell-ID`, `sS-RSRP`, `sS-RSRQ`, `cSI-RSRP`, `cSI-RSRQ`, `angleOfArrivalNR`, `timingAdvanceNR`, or `uE-Rx-Tx-Time-Diff`. No duplicates allowed.
  - `eutra` (array of strings, optional): Used when the serving cell is E-UTRA. Each entry must be one of `cell-ID`, `angleOfArrival`, `timingAdvanceType1`, `timingAdvanceType2`, `rSRP`, or `rSRQ`. No duplicates allowed.

### Responses

| Status | Condition                                                                                      |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `200`  | Returns a location estimate.                                                                   |
| `403`  | The subscriber is a [roamer](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/roaming/#roamers). |
| `404`  | Subscriber not registered, or no estimate.                                                     |
| `504`  | Location request timed out.                                                                    |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "locationEstimate": {
            "shape": "POINT_UNCERTAINTY_CIRCLE",
            "point": {
                "lat": 37.7749,
                "lon": -122.4194
            },
            "uncertainty": 150
        },
        "positioningDataList": [
            {
                "method": "CELLID",
                "mode": "CONVENTIONAL",
                "usage": "SUCCESS_RESULTS_USED_TO_GENERATE_LOCATION"
            }
        ],
        "ncgi": {
            "plmnId": {
                "mcc": "001",
                "mnc": "01"
            },
            "nrCellId": "000000010"
        }
    }
}
```

### Sample Response (`ecid`)

```
{
    "result": {
        "locationEstimate": {
            "shape": "POINT_UNCERTAINTY_CIRCLE",
            "point": {
                "lat": 37.7749,
                "lon": -122.4194
            },
            "uncertainty": 150
        },
        "positioningDataList": [
            {
                "method": "CELLID",
                "mode": "CONVENTIONAL",
                "usage": "SUCCESS_RESULTS_USED_TO_GENERATE_LOCATION"
            },
            {
                "method": "NR_ECID",
                "mode": "CONVENTIONAL",
                "usage": "UNSUCCESS"
            },
            {
                "method": "NR_ECID",
                "mode": "UE_ASSISTED",
                "usage": "SUCCESS_RESULTS_NOT_USED"
            }
        ],
        "ncgi": {
            "plmnId": {
                "mcc": "001",
                "mnc": "01"
            },
            "nrCellId": "000000010"
        },
        "radioMeasurements": [
            {
                "source": "UE",
                "rat": "NR",
                "serving": true,
                "pci": 180,
                "arfcn": 662592,
                "arfcnType": "SSB",
                "ssRsrp": -84,
                "ssRsrq": -11,
                "ssbBeams": [
                    {
                        "index": 0,
                        "rsrp": -84,
                        "rsrq": -11
                    }
                ]
            },
            {
                "source": "UE",
                "rat": "EUTRA",
                "serving": false,
                "pci": 148,
                "arfcn": 9310,
                "rsrp": -98,
                "rsrq": -7.5
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

## Create a Deferred Location Request

This path starts periodic location reporting for a subscriber (TS 23.273 deferred location request).

| Method | Path                                   |
| ------ | -------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/beta/location/deferred-requests` |

### Parameters

- `supi` (string): Subscriber identity.
- `ldr_type` (string): One of `UE_AVAILABLE`, `PERIODIC`, `ENTERING_INTO_AREA`, `LEAVING_FROM_AREA`, `BEING_INSIDE_AREA`, or `MOTION`. Only `PERIODIC` is supported.
- `periodic_event_info` (object):
  - `reporting_amount` (integer): Number of reports, 1 to 8639999. Required unless `reporting_infinite_ind` is `true`.
  - `reporting_interval` (integer): Interval between reports in seconds, 1 to 8639999. `reporting_amount` x `reporting_interval` must not exceed 8639999.
  - `reporting_infinite_ind` (boolean, optional): Report until 8639999 seconds have elapsed.
  - `reporting_interval_ms` (integer, optional): 1 to 999. Not supported; `reporting_interval` is used.
- `scheduled_loc_time` (string, optional): RFC 3339 time of the first report. Must be in the future.
- `method` (string, optional): `cell_id`, `ecid`, or `gnss`. Defaults to `cell_id`.
- `mode` (string, optional): `network_based` or `ue_assisted` for `ecid`; `standalone` for `gnss`. Defaults to every mode supported by `method`.
- `measurement_quantities` (object, optional): As in [Locate a Subscriber](#locate-a-subscriber).

### Responses

| Status | Condition                                                                                      |
| ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `201`  | Returns the deferred location request.                                                         |
| `400`  | Invalid parameters.                                                                            |
| `403`  | The subscriber is a [roamer](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/roaming/#roamers). |
| `404`  | Subscriber not registered on this node.                                                        |
| `409`  | The subscriber already has an active deferred location request.                                |
| `501`  | `ldr_type` is not supported.                                                                   |
| `503`  | Deferred location requests are unavailable.                                                    |

### Sample Request

```
{
    "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
    "ldr_type": "PERIODIC",
    "periodic_event_info": {
        "reporting_amount": 120,
        "reporting_interval": 30
    },
    "method": "ecid",
    "mode": "network_based"
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": "019a2f3c-8d1e-7b2a-9c4f-1e2d3c4b5a69",
        "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
        "ldr_type": "PERIODIC",
        "periodic_event_info": {
            "reporting_amount": 120,
            "reporting_interval": 30
        },
        "method": "ecid",
        "mode": "network_based",
        "status": "ACTIVE",
        "created_at": "2026-10-15T14:00:00Z"
    }
}
```

## List Deferred Location Requests

This path returns a paginated list of deferred location requests, newest first.

| Method | Path                                   |
| ------ | -------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/beta/location/deferred-requests` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed                | Description          |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ---------------------- | -------------------- |
| `supi`     | query | str  |         |                        | Subscriber identity. |
| `status`   | query | str  |         | `ACTIVE`, `TERMINATED` | Request status.      |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`                 | Page number.         |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1..100`               | Items per page.      |

### Response Fields

| Field                    | Type    | Description                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                     | string  | Request identifier.                                                                         |
| `supi`                   | string  | Subscriber identity.                                                                        |
| `ldr_type`               | string  | `PERIODIC`.                                                                                 |
| `periodic_event_info`    | object  | Accepted reporting parameters.                                                              |
| `scheduled_loc_time`     | string  | Time of the first report.                                                                   |
| `method`                 | string  | Positioning method.                                                                         |
| `mode`                   | string  | Positioning mode.                                                                           |
| `measurement_quantities` | object  | E-CID measurement quantities.                                                               |
| `status`                 | string  | `ACTIVE` or `TERMINATED`.                                                                   |
| `termination_cause`      | string  | `NORMAL_TERMINATION`, `TERMINATION_BY_UE`, or `TERMINATION_BY_NETWORK` (TS 29.572).         |
| `termination_reason`     | string  | `ue_deregistered`, `ue_mobility`, `positioning_failed`, `node_restart`, or `node_shutdown`. |
| `event_report_counter`   | integer | Number of reports produced (TS 29.572). Absent before the first report.                     |
| `created_at`             | string  | Creation time.                                                                              |
| `terminated_at`          | string  | Termination time.                                                                           |

Terminated requests and their reports are deleted 7 days after termination. Each request keeps its 10000 most recent reports.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": "019a2f3c-8d1e-7b2a-9c4f-1e2d3c4b5a69",
                "supi": "imsi-001010000000001",
                "ldr_type": "PERIODIC",
                "periodic_event_info": {
                    "reporting_amount": 120,
                    "reporting_interval": 30
                },
                "method": "ecid",
                "mode": "network_based",
                "status": "TERMINATED",
                "termination_cause": "TERMINATION_BY_NETWORK",
                "termination_reason": "ue_deregistered",
                "event_report_counter": 42,
                "created_at": "2026-10-15T14:00:00Z",
                "terminated_at": "2026-10-15T14:21:03.512Z"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}
```

## Get a Deferred Location Request

This path returns a deferred location request.

| Method | Path                                        |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/beta/location/deferred-requests/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type   | Description         |
| ---- | ------ | ------------------- |
| `id` | string | Request identifier. |

The response fields are those of [List Deferred Location Requests](#list-deferred-location-requests).

## Delete a Deferred Location Request

This path stops a deferred location request if it is active, then deletes it and its reports.

| Method | Path                                        |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| DELETE | `/api/beta/location/deferred-requests/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type   | Description         |
| ---- | ------ | ------------------- |
| `id` | string | Request identifier. |

Returns `200 OK` on success.

## List Location Reports

This path returns the location reports of a deferred location request, oldest first.

| Method | Path                                                |
| ------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/beta/location/deferred-requests/{id}/reports` |

### Query Parameters

| Name    | In    | Type | Default | Allowed   | Description                          |
| ------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | --------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `after` | query | int  | `0`     | `>= 0`    | Return reports with a greater `seq`. |
| `limit` | query | int  | `100`   | `1..1000` | Maximum number of reports.           |

### Response Fields

| Field                   | Type    | Description                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `items[].seq`           | integer | Report number, starting at 1.                                                  |
| `items[].reported_at`   | string  | Report time.                                                                   |
| `items[].location_data` | object  | Location estimate, as returned by [Locate a Subscriber](#locate-a-subscriber). |
| `next`                  | integer | Value to pass as `after` for the following reports.                            |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "seq": 1,
                "reported_at": "2026-10-15T14:00:00.812Z",
                "location_data": {
                    "locationEstimate": {
                        "shape": "POINT_UNCERTAINTY_CIRCLE",
                        "point": {
                            "lat": 37.7749,
                            "lon": -122.4194
                        },
                        "uncertainty": 50
                    },
                    "positioningDataList": [
                        {
                            "method": "NR_ECID",
                            "mode": "CONVENTIONAL",
                            "usage": "SUCCESS_RESULTS_USED_TO_GENERATE_LOCATION"
                        }
                    ]
                }
            }
        ],
        "next": 1
    }
}
```

## List Cell Positions

This path returns all provisioned cell positions.

| Method | Path                       |
| ------ | -------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/beta/cell-positions` |

### Response Fields

| Field                    | Type    | Description                                            |
| ------------------------ | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`                     | string  | Cell position identifier.                              |
| `rat`                    | string  | `nr` or `eutra`.                                       |
| `mcc`                    | string  | Mobile Country Code.                                   |
| `mnc`                    | string  | Mobile Network Code.                                   |
| `cell_identity`          | string  | Hex cell identity (NCI for NR, ECI for E-UTRA).        |
| `gnb_id`                 | string  | gNB identifier.                                        |
| `latitude`               | number  | WGS-84 latitude in decimal degrees.                    |
| `longitude`              | number  | WGS-84 longitude in decimal degrees.                   |
| `altitude`               | number  | Altitude, in metres.                                   |
| `uncertainty_semi_major` | number  | Semi-major axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres. |
| `uncertainty_semi_minor` | number  | Semi-minor axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres. |
| `orientation_major`      | integer | Orientation of the semi-major axis, in degrees.        |
| `confidence`             | integer | Confidence, in percent.                                |
| `source`                 | string  | Origin of the record (e.g. `provisioned`).             |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": [
        {
            "id": "018f9f3a-4c2e-7bd1-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
            "rat": "nr",
            "mcc": "001",
            "mnc": "01",
            "cell_identity": "000000010",
            "latitude": 37.7749,
            "longitude": -122.4194,
            "source": "provisioned"
        }
    ]
}
```

## Create a Cell Position

This path provisions the geographic position of a cell antenna. Cell ID lookups resolve a subscriber's serving cell to this position.

| Method | Path                       |
| ------ | -------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/beta/cell-positions` |

### Parameters

- `rat` (string): `nr` or `eutra`.
- `mcc` (string): Mobile Country Code.
- `mnc` (string): Mobile Network Code.
- `cell_identity` (string): Hex cell identity (NCI for NR, ECI for E-UTRA).
- `gnb_id` (string, optional): gNB identifier.
- `latitude` (number): WGS-84 latitude in decimal degrees. Range `-90`…`90`.
- `longitude` (number): WGS-84 longitude in decimal degrees. Range `-180`…`180`.
- `altitude` (number, optional): Altitude, in metres.
- `uncertainty_semi_major` (number, optional): Semi-major axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres.
- `uncertainty_semi_minor` (number, optional): Semi-minor axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres.
- `orientation_major` (integer, optional): Orientation of the semi-major axis, in degrees.
- `confidence` (integer, optional): Confidence, in percent.

### Sample Request (E-UTRA)

```
{
    "rat": "eutra",
    "mcc": "001",
    "mnc": "01",
    "cell_identity": "0000001",
    "latitude": 37.7749,
    "longitude": -122.4194
}
```

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Cell position created",
        "id": "018f9f3a-4c2e-7bd1-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f"
    }
}
```

## Get a Cell Position

This path returns a provisioned cell position.

| Method | Path                            |

| GET    | `/api/beta/cell-positions/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type   | Description               |

```
{
    "result": {
        "id": "018f9f3a-4c2e-7bd1-9f21-0a1b2c3d4e5f",
```

## Update a Cell Position

This path updates a provisioned cell position.

| Method | Path                            |
| ------ | ------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/beta/cell-positions/{id}` |

### Path Parameters

| Name | Type   | Description               |
| ---- | ------ | ------------------------- |
| `id` | string | Cell position identifier. |

### Parameters

- `rat` (string): `nr` or `eutra`.
- `mcc` (string): Mobile Country Code.
- `mnc` (string): Mobile Network Code.
- `cell_identity` (string): Hex cell identity (NCI for NR, ECI for E-UTRA).
- `gnb_id` (string, optional): gNB identifier.
- `latitude` (number): WGS-84 latitude in decimal degrees. Range `-90`…`90`.
- `longitude` (number): WGS-84 longitude in decimal degrees. Range `-180`…`180`.
- `altitude` (number, optional): Altitude, in metres.
- `uncertainty_semi_major` (number, optional): Semi-major axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres.
- `uncertainty_semi_minor` (number, optional): Semi-minor axis of the uncertainty ellipse, in metres.
- `orientation_major` (integer, optional): Orientation of the semi-major axis, in degrees.
- `confidence` (integer, optional): Confidence, in percent.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Cell position updated"
    }
}
```

None

```
# HELP go_gc_gogc_percent Heap size target percentage configured by the user, otherwise 100. This value is set by the GOGC environment variable, and the runtime/debug.SetGCPercent function. Sourced from /gc/gogc:percent

go_gc_gogc_percent 100
...
```

# Data Networks

## List Data Networks

This path returns the list of data networks.

| Method | Path                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "name": "internet",
                "ipv4_pool": "172.250.0.0/24",
                "ipv6_pool": "2001:db8::/48",
                "dns": "8.8.8.8",
                "mtu": 1460,
                "ims": false,
                "status": {
                    "sessions": 0
                }
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 10,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}
```

## Create a Data Network

This path creates a new Data Network.

| Method | Path                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks` |

### Parameters

- `name` (string): The Name of the Data Network (dnn)
- `ipv4_pool` (string, optional): The IPv4 pool of the data network in CIDR notation. Example: `172.250.0.0/24`. At least one of `ipv4_pool` or `ipv6_pool` must be provided.
- `ipv6_pool` (string, optional): The IPv6 pool of the data network in CIDR notation. Example: `2001:db8::/48`.
- `dns` (string): The IP address of the DNS server of the data network. Example: `8.8.8.8`.
- `mtu` (integer): The MTU of the data network. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
- `ims` (boolean, optional): Whether this is an IMS data network. Defaults to `true` for a data network named `ims`, `false` otherwise. See [IMS Integration](https://docs.ellanetworks.com/core/explanation/ims_integration/index.md).

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Data Network created successfully"
    }
}
```

## Update a Data Network

This path updates an existing data network.

| Method | Path                                      |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks/{name}` |

### Parameters

- `ipv4_pool` (string, optional): The IPv4 pool of the data network in CIDR notation. Example: `172.250.0.0/24`. At least one of `ipv4_pool` or `ipv6_pool` must be provided.
- `ipv6_pool` (string, optional): The IPv6 pool of the data network in CIDR notation. Example: `2001:db8::/48`.
- `dns` (string): The IP address of the DNS server of the data network. Example: `8.8.8.8`.
- `mtu` (integer): The MTU of the data network. Must be an integer between 1 and 65535.
- `ims` (boolean, optional): Whether this is an IMS data network. Enabling it requires every policy on the data network to use 5QI 5 or 69. Changing it releases the data network's sessions so that UEs reconnect. Omitted leaves it unchanged.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Data Network updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Get a Data Network

This path returns the details of a specific data network.

| Method | Path                                      |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks/{name}` |

## Create a Static IP

### Parameters

```
    "result": {

    }
}
```

## Update a Static IP

This path repins a subscriber's reservation to a new address. A change to a live session releases it so the UE re-establishes on the new address.

| Method | Path                                                                     |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks/{name}/static-ips/{imsi}/{ip_version}` |

### Parameters

- `address` (string): The new IPv4 address or /64-aligned IPv6 prefix within the data network pool. Example: `172.250.0.20`.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Static IP updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Delete a Static IP

This path removes a subscriber's static IP reservation. A change to a live session releases it so the UE re-establishes on a dynamic address.

| Method | Path                                                                     |

### Parameters

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Static IP deleted successfully"
    }
}
```

## List Framed Routes

This path returns the framed routes for a specific data network, grouped by subscriber. A framed route is an IP prefix routed toward a subscriber's session, so a whole subnet behind the UE is reachable over one session.

| Method | Path                                                    |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks/{name}/framed-routes` |

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "imsi": "001010100000001",
                "ipv4": ["192.168.60.0/24"],
                "ipv6": ["fd00:60::/64"]
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 1,
        "total_count": 1
    }
}
```

## Create Framed Routes

This path sets a subscriber's framed-route set on a data network. At most 8 prefixes per family are allowed, and each is masked to its network form.

| Method | Path                                                    |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks/{name}/framed-routes` |

### Parameters

- `imsi` (string): The IMSI of the subscriber.
- `ipv4` (array of strings): IPv4 framed-route prefixes in CIDR form. Example: `["192.168.60.0/24"]`.
- `ipv6` (array of strings): IPv6 framed-route prefixes in CIDR form. Example: `["fd00:60::/64"]`.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Framed routes created successfully"
    }
}
```

## Update Framed Routes

This path replaces a subscriber's entire framed-route set on a data network. A change to a live session releases it so the UE re-establishes with the new routes.

| Method | Path                                                           |
| ------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/networking/data-networks/{name}/framed-routes/{imsi}` |

### Parameters

- `ipv4` (array of strings): The replacement IPv4 framed-route prefixes in CIDR form.
- `ipv6` (array of strings): The replacement IPv6 framed-route prefixes in CIDR form.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Framed routes updated successfully"
    }
}
```

## Delete Framed Routes

This path removes all framed routes for a subscriber on a data network.

| Method | Path                                                           |

### Parameters

### Parameters

None

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "n2": {
            "addresses": ["192.168.40.6"],
            "port": 38412,
            "interface": "eth0"
        },
        "n3": {
            "name": "wlp131s0",
            "addresses": ["192.168.40.6"],
            "external_address": ""
        },
        "n6": {
            "name": "lo",
            "addresses": ["10.0.0.1"]
        },
        "api": {
            "addresses": ["192.168.1.10"],
            "port": 5002
        },
        "diameter": {
            "addresses": ["10.0.0.10"],
            "port": 3868
        },
        "n32": {
            "addresses": ["10.0.0.20"],
            "port": 443,
            "interface": "ens5"
        }
    }
}
```

## Update N3 Interface Settings

This path updates the N3 interface settings.

| Method | Path                               |
| ------ | ---------------------------------- |
| PUT    | `/api/v1/networking/interfaces/n3` |

### Parameters

- `external_address` (string): The external address to be used for the N3 / S1-U interface: an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address, or one of each separated by a comma. This address is advertised to the radio in the GTP tunnel Transport Layer Address. The radio uses it to set up the GTP-U tunnel. This setting is useful when Ella Core is behind a proxy or NAT and the N3 / S1-U interface address is not reachable by the radio. If not set, Ella Core will use the address of the N3 interface as defined in the config file.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "N3 interface updated"
    }
}
```

# Routes

## List Routes

This path returns the list of routes, including both user-configured static routes and BGP-learned routes. Each route includes a `source` field indicating its origin (`static` or `bgp`).

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| GET    | `/api/v1/networking/routes` |

### Query Parameters

| Name       | In    | Type | Default | Allowed | Description               |
| ---------- | ----- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ------------------------- |
| `page`     | query | int  | `1`     | `>= 1`  | 1-based page index.       |
| `per_page` | query | int  | `25`    | `1…100` | Number of items per page. |

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "items": [
            {
                "id": 0,
                "destination": "0.0.0.0/0",
                "gateway": "10.0.0.2",
                "interface": "n6",
                "metric": 200,
                "source": "bgp"
            },
            {
                "id": 1,
                "destination": "10.0.0.0/24",
                "gateway": "203.0.113.1",
                "interface": "n6",
                "metric": 0,
                "source": "static"
            },
            {
                "id": 2,
                "destination": "::/0",
                "gateway": "2001:db8::1",
                "interface": "n6",
                "metric": 200,
                "source": "bgp"
            },
            {
                "id": 3,
                "destination": "fd45::/48",
                "gateway": "2001:db8:6::2",
                "interface": "n6",
                "metric": 0,
                "source": "static"
            }
        ],
        "page": 1,
        "per_page": 25,
        "total_count": 4
    }
}
```

## Create a Route

This path creates a new route.

| Method | Path                        |
| ------ | --------------------------- |
| POST   | `/api/v1/networking/routes` |

### Parameters

- `destination` (string): The destination IP address of the route in CIDR notation. Examples: `0.0.0.0/0` (IPv4) or `::/0` (IPv6).
- `gateway` (string): The IP address of the gateway of the route. Examples: `1.2.3.4` (IPv4) or `2001:db8::1` (IPv6).
- `interface` (string): The outgoing interface of the route. Allowed values: `n3`, `n6`.
- `metric` (int): The metric of the route. Must be a non-negative integer.

### Sample Response

```
{
    "result": {
        "message": "Route created successfully",
        "id": "4"
    }
}
```
